feed.title: Smart Water for a Smarter Home: Moen Leads the Way with Industry's First Whole-Home Connected Water Product Suite
feed.summary: Moen introduces the industry's first whole-home smart water ecosystem, the Moen Smart Water Network, which allows consumers to control, monitor, and conserve water throughout their homes using a single smartphone app. The network includes new and expanded smart products like the Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff, Smart Leak Detector, Smart Sump Pump Monitor, Smart Faucet with Motion Control, and Smart Shower, all designed to provide peace of mind, security, and personalized water experiences. These innovations offer automated water security, water usage education, personalized settings, and voice activation capabilities for a truly connected home water system.

feed.title: Best Buy Launches New Advertising Business, Best Buy Ads
feed.summary: Best Buy has launched Best Buy Ads, a new in-house media company, to help shoppers discover products and services by leveraging its deep customer insights and interactions. The initiative also aims to address diversity and inclusion in the advertising industry by dedicating part of its media spend to BIPOC media and launching a Career Pathways program for teens from underrepresented backgrounds. This move diversifies Best Buy's business and creates equitable opportunities within the advertising sector.

feed.title: 7 payments trends for 2022 as innovation climbs
feed.summary: The payments industry is facing rapid innovation and competition in 2022, driven by the ongoing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic which accelerated the adoption of digital payments. Key trends include the simmering dispute between Amazon and Visa over merchant transaction fees, the expansion of Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) services into B2B, the growing adoption of mobile wallets, and the increasing demand for cross-border payment services. Additionally, central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) are gaining prominence over cryptocurrencies, while cybersecurity is becoming an urgent priority due to rising fraud, and regulators are increasing scrutiny on big tech payment platforms and emerging fintechs.

feed.title: Kroger expanding into Oklahoma City as it builds national delivery network
feed.summary: Kroger is re-entering the Oklahoma City market after a long absence, not by opening physical stores, but by establishing a warehouse and office space to support its national delivery network. This expansion is part of a broader partnership with Ocado to build automated customer fulfillment centers that utilize AI and robotics for efficient grocery delivery. The move aims to extend Kroger's e-commerce reach and provide delivery services to new and existing markets, leveraging a hub-and-spoke model.

feed.title: FLASHBACK: Stormy Outlook For Sea Limited (SE) After Stock Sell Off?
feed.summary: This article revisits an analysis from January 2022 by Hedgeye's China analyst, Felix Wang, who flagged Sea Limited (SE) as a "Best Idea Short" a month prior. Wang argued that despite its past growth, SE faced increasing competition in gaming and e-commerce, a smaller total addressable market than commonly believed, and an overvalued stock. He projected at least an additional 20% downside for the stock based on his 2023 sum-of-the-parts valuation.

feed.title: Amazon, Stellantis Team Up on Software, Delivery Vehicles
feed.summary: Amazon (AMZN) and Stellantis (STLA) are collaborating on software development and electric delivery vehicles. Amazon will use Stellantis' upcoming Ram ProMaster electric delivery van, making it the first commercial customer for the vehicle, and the partnership will also involve digital technology and cloud services. This move positions Stellantis as a competitor to Rivian Automotive Inc. in supplying EVs to Amazon.

feed.title: Stellantis taps Amazon to bolster software plans, will sell it EV vans
feed.summary: Stellantis announced a multi-year partnership with Amazon to enhance its software-driven vehicle offerings and services. The collaboration includes deploying Amazon software in Stellantis vehicles, training engineers, and making Amazon the first commercial customer for the battery-electric Ram ProMaster van. This move aims to significantly increase Stellantis's annual revenue from software-enabled products and subscriptions by 2030, transforming the automaker into a technologically savvy mobility company.

feed.title: Shares in Future Group firms fall as court dismisses appeal
feed.summary: Shares in several Future Group companies declined after an Indian court dismissed Future Retail's appeal to declare arbitration proceedings with Amazon.com Inc. illegal. This legal dispute is part of a larger struggle between Amazon and Reliance Industries for control over assets of the Future Group in the competitive Indian retail market. Future Retail has since filed another appeal in the Delhi High Court.

feed.title: Behind Best Buy’s New In-House Ad Venture
feed.summary: Best Buy has launched "Best Buy Ads," an in-house media company that leverages its extensive customer data to help partner brands create personalized ad messages. This move is a strategic evolution of its existing Best Buy Media Network, aiming to create a new revenue stream and capitalize on the valuable customer data Best Buy collects. The initiative mirrors similar efforts by other large retailers like Target and Amazon, driven by the desire to monetize data and enhance targeted advertising.

feed.title: GE, Boston Scientific team up to bring advanced cardiac care tech to Southeast Asia
feed.summary: GE Healthcare and Boston Scientific have partnered to enhance cardiac care in Southeast Asia by combining GE's imaging software with Boston Scientific's heart-focused medical devices. This collaboration aims to address the high number of cardiovascular disease deaths in the region by providing advanced tools for diagnosis and interventional treatments. This partnership is part of GE Healthcare's broader strategy as it prepares to become a standalone company by early 2023.

feed.title: Live Nation Backs Liquid Death In New $75 Million Funding Round
feed.summary: Live Nation has once again invested in Liquid Death, a canned water company, through a new $75 million Series C funding round. This brings Liquid Death's total funding to $125 million and values the brand at $525 million. The funding will further support the growth of Liquid Death, which has significantly increased its distribution and revenue, leveraging its exclusivity at Live Nation venues and festivals.

feed.title: Amazon makes deal with Stellantis for electric delivery vehicles
feed.summary: Amazon has partnered with Stellantis for software collaboration and become the first customer for a new Ram electric delivery vehicle. This deal builds on an existing relationship where Stellantis has supplied Amazon with tens of thousands of delivery vehicles since 2018. The move highlights Amazon's ongoing investment in electric vehicle technology and its collaborations within the automotive industry.

feed.title: Stryker ponies up $3B to buy Vocera and amp up its digital communications
feed.summary: Stryker has announced a $3 billion acquisition of Vocera Communications to enhance its digital patient outreach and communication efforts. Vocera's portfolio, including smartphone apps, workflow analytics, and communication hardware, will be integrated to link Stryker's medical devices and boost care coordination, especially in remote settings. The deal, valued at $3.09 billion including convertible notes, is expected to close by the end of March.

feed.title: Marin Software Announces Amazon DSP Integration to Expand Amazon Advertising Solutions
feed.summary: Marin Software announced an integration with Amazon Ads' demand-side platform (DSP), allowing brands to manage, measure, and optimize their Amazon Advertising campaigns within the MarinOne platform. This integration expands Marin Software's offerings to include display, video, and audio ads, enabling advertisers to reach Amazon audiences at scale across various platforms. The expanded suite of tools helps advertisers drive higher efficiency and transparency in their Amazon advertising programs, connecting upper-funnel ad spend with in-store purchases.

feed.title: Machine Customers Will Decide Who Gets Their Trillion-Dollar Business. Is It You?
feed.summary: The article explores the rise of "machine customers" and their potential to drive a trillion-dollar business opportunity. It outlines how these nonhuman entities, ranging from bound to autonomous customers, make purchasing decisions differently from humans by being transparent, processing vast amounts of data, and prioritizing efficiency over emotional loyalty. Businesses must adapt their corporate strategy, sales, marketing, and data analytics to cater to this evolving market.

feed.title: Lululemon Hires Amazon Exec to Lead Mirror as Nike Lawsuit Looms
feed.summary: Lululemon has hired Amazon veteran Michael Aragon to lead its interactive home gym business, Mirror, amidst a patent infringement lawsuit filed by Nike. Aragon, formerly chief content officer at Twitch, will oversee Mirror's development and expansion, reporting directly to Lululemon's CEO Calvin McDonald. This move signifies Lululemon's commitment to Mirror, despite facing headwinds and a legal challenge from Nike concerning its digital fitness technology.

feed.title: Google loses Sonos smart speakers patent fight
feed.summary: Smart-speaker firm Sonos has won a major legal battle against Google, with the US International Trade Commission ruling that Google infringed on five of Sonos' patents related to multi-room audio technology. This decision could lead to a ban on importing infringing Google smart home tech into the United States, and Sonos suggests Google may have to "degrade" its products or pay licensing fees. Google disputes the ruling, stating it has already developed workarounds and does not expect the decision to impact its ability to sell products.

feed.title: The Best Wi-Fi Routers
feed.summary: This article reviews the best Wi-Fi routers for different needs, including top picks for most households, mesh systems, enthusiasts, and budget-conscious buyers. It highlights specific models like the Asus RT-AX3000, Netgear Orbi RBK50/RBK752, Asus RT-AX88U, and Netgear R6700 Nighthawk AC1750, providing pricing, performance details, and use case recommendations for each. The authors also discuss the shift towards Wi-Fi 6 systems and the benefits of mesh networks over traditional routers with range extenders.

feed.title: Updating My Favorite Performance Chart For 2021
feed.summary: Ben Carlson updates his asset allocation quilt for 2021, analyzing the performance of various asset classes over the last decade. He highlights REITs' surprising strong performance, the ongoing struggles of commodities despite recent gains, and the consistent outperformance of the S&P 500. The article also discusses the impact of diversification and the impressive long-term returns of U.S. stocks even when including the 2008 financial crisis.

feed.title: Tech Moves: Adaptive CFO to resign; Meta comms exec departs; AI vet joins Absci board; new Zymeworks CEO
feed.summary: This article details several significant personnel changes in the tech and biotech sectors, including Chad Cohen's resignation as CFO of Adaptive Biotechnologies, Joseph Sirosh's appointment to the Absci board, John Pinette's departure from Meta, and Kenneth Galbraith becoming the new CEO of Zymeworks. It highlights the impact of these moves on the respective companies and their financial performance or strategic direction.

feed.title: Payments firms see slam dunk opportunity with sports venues
feed.summary: The sports and events industry is becoming a major focus for digital payments companies, which are introducing new technologies to enhance the fan experience and gather valuable data. The push for cashless and contactless transactions was accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to the adoption of mobile ordering, self-service kiosks, and checkout-free options in stadiums and arenas. These advancements not only speed up transactions but also provide venues with crucial insights into fan behavior and purchasing habits.

feed.title: Behind Lineage’s innovative solar plus ‘linear generator’ installation
feed.summary: Lineage Logistics has implemented an innovative solar array paired with linear generators at its Colton Agua Mansa, California facility, allowing it to generate 100 percent of its energy consumption onsite, significantly reducing grid dependency and operating costs. This installation, among the first of its kind, helps the company achieve its commitment to net-zero carbon by 2040 as a signatory to The Climate Pledge. The success of this project establishes a scalable template for Lineage to expand similar sustainable energy solutions across its global network.

feed.title: Introducing Zero100, a New Community for Operations Leaders and Their Teams, Exploring the Intersection of Supply Chain and Technology in the Climate Era
feed.summary: Zero100 has launched a new community-based education and research platform aimed at operations and supply chain leaders. The platform focuses on achieving "Zero Percent Carbon, 100% Digital" supply chains by fostering collaboration, providing data-driven research, and offering learning programs. Founded by leaders from major tech and retail companies and backed by personal investments, Zero100 seeks to modernize the supply chain profession in the climate era.

feed.title: Amazon Delivery Drivers Sprint After Rolling Delivery Vans
feed.summary: The article discusses the issue of Mercedes Sprinter vans, primarily used by Amazon delivery drivers, rolling away despite being placed in park. It details a NHTSA investigation into the problem, attributing potential causes to a defective park pawl rather than driver error, and criticizes Mercedes-Benz's response which largely blames drivers while proposing a software fix and a temporary horn alert. The piece highlights the intense work conditions of Amazon drivers and questions the effectiveness and fairness of Mercedes' proposed solutions given the mechanical weaknesses identified.

feed.title: Stryker buy of Vocera to aid confluence of communication, devices
feed.summary: Stryker Corp. is acquiring Vocera Communications for over $3 billion, marking a significant entry into the healthcare technology space. This acquisition aims to integrate medical devices and communication capabilities, intending to improve efficiencies for care teams and enhance patient experiences. The deal is expected to create a confluence of devices, intelligence, and communication in healthcare, with potential future applications in chronic and ambulatory care models.

feed.title: Retail Brew
feed.summary: Catrice Cosmetics has ended its partnership with Ulta to focus solely on direct-to-consumer and Amazon sales, aiming for better shopper connection and sales growth. Meanwhile, a new report highlights that nearly all shoppers are less likely to buy from a brand again after a poor returns experience, underscoring the critical need for optimized return processes as e-commerce grows. Additionally, JD.com has launched robot-powered retail stores in the Netherlands, marking its first European expansion and enhancing robotic fulfillment in retail.

feed.title: 194 IMT Hyderabad PGDM students placed; highest CTC is Rs 16 lakh per annum
feed.summary: IMT Hyderabad's 2021 placement drive saw 194 out of 198 PGDM students placed, with the highest annual salary reaching Rs 16 lakh and an average of Rs 9.28 lakh. The consulting sector was the top recruiter, attracting 45 participating companies including giants like Amazon, Deloitte, and Marico. The institute also published data on top offers and sector-wise recruitment percentages, along with its NIRF ranking.

feed.title: Welcoming the Post-Zoom Era
feed.summary: The article discusses the impending end of the "Zoom era," noting a waning enthusiasm for constant video conferencing, even among those previously reliant on it. Author Jonathan Bartlett observes that people are increasingly opting out of Zoom meetings and classes, highlighting the draining nature of online interaction compared to in-person engagement. He suggests that organizations must soon decide whether to be primarily remote or in-person, and for remote setups, managers will need to minimize Zoom time and find alternative ways to foster team cohesion to prevent a decline in loyalty.

feed.title: Best Buy Co. Inc. stock falls Wednesday, underperforms market
feed.summary: Best Buy Co. Inc. (BBY) stock declined by 1.35% on Wednesday, closing at $102.68, while the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average saw gains. This fall ended a two-day winning streak for Best Buy, leaving it significantly below its 52-week high. The stock also underperformed key competitors including Apple and Amazon.com, which rose or had smaller declines, respectively.

feed.title: Tuvalu: Strikes deal with GoDaddy to manage .tv - ABC Pacific
feed.summary: Tuvalu has signed a new deal with US internet giant GoDaddy to manage its valuable .tv domain name, expecting a significant increase in revenue from the previous US$5 million per year received from Verisign. The .tv domain's value has surged due to its association with streaming platforms like Twitch, ensuring a key revenue source for the Pacific Island nation. The Tuvalu Telecommunications Corporation aims for greater benefits for its people and economy from this new agreement.

feed.title: Tickets for D23 Expo: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event Presented by Visa® Go on Sale January 20, 2022
feed.summary: Tickets for D23 Expo 2022, presented by Visa, will go on sale January 20, 2022, with a presale for Visa cardholders who are also D23 Members starting January 19. The event, hosted by D23: The Official Disney Fan Club, will take place September 9-11 at the Anaheim Convention Center, celebrating Disney entertainment and kicking off Disney100, the company's centennial celebration. It will feature over 50 shows, presentations, and panels, including the Disney Legends Awards Ceremony, the Mousequerade costume contest, and an exhibit of Walt Disney's restored Grumman Gulfstream I company airplane.

feed.title: Lloyds aims to save £800m with shift to cloud, DXC to lead modernisation
feed.summary: Lloyd's, a major insurance marketplace, has launched an ambitious digital transformation program called "Future at Lloyd's" to move core applications to the cloud and digitize paper-based processes. DXC Technology has been selected as the lead IT provider, with AWS as the primary cloud provider. This initiative is expected to save £800 million in operating costs for brokers, underwriters, and partners.

feed.title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems
feed.summary: This article analyzes the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems, highlighting key market trends and changes from the previous report. It details Gartner's definition of the market, significant additions and removals of vendors, and the evolving positions of major players like Amazon, Microsoft, Oracle, Google, Snowflake, and Databricks within the Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players quadrants. The report emphasizes the increasing shift to cloud platforms, the impact of multicloud strategies, and the growing importance of various data models and use cases in the CDBMS market.

feed.title: Kroger levels up autonomous delivery with Nuro’s commercial-grade vehicles
feed.summary: Kroger announced a partnership with tech firm Nuro to begin using Nuro's third-generation autonomous vehicles for grocery deliveries in Houston, Texas. These new electric vehicles offer double the cargo volume, customized storage, and advanced temperature control compared to previous models. This initiative is part of Kroger's broader strategy to integrate automation into its online shopping experience, aiming to reduce long-term costs and improve efficiency.

feed.title: Behind the Scenes With Cigna Ventures: Giving Great Ideas the Momentum To Make an Impact
feed.summary: Cigna Ventures, the strategic venture fund of Cigna Corporation, focuses on improving health care affordability, simplicity, and predictability by partnering with innovative entrepreneurs. The fund invests across three key areas: Health Care Insights and Analytics, Digital Health and Experiences, and Care Delivery and Enablement. Through these investments, Cigna Ventures aims to accelerate Cigna's strategy, bring innovation into the organization, and bring differentiated value to Cigna customers and the healthcare system.

feed.title: How retailers can meet consumers’ growing demand for sustainability and hybrid shopping experiences
feed.summary: A new global study from IBM IBV and NRF reveals that consumer preferences have shifted significantly, with a growing demand for hybrid shopping experiences and sustainability. Retailers must adapt by offering personalized experiences, transparent supply chains, and agile operations, leveraging technologies like AI and hybrid cloud. While consumers express a willingness to pay more for sustainable products, there's still a gap between their intentions and actual purchasing behavior, which can be addressed through greater transparency.

feed.title: As Stellantis turns 1, automaker faces two paths
feed.summary: As Stellantis marks its first anniversary, experts predict two potential futures for the automaker: becoming a strong EV player like Ford or facing challenges similar to GM decades ago. Despite a strategic focus on electrification through partnerships and investments, the company has yet to launch a fully electric vehicle in North America and struggles with underutilized plants and profitability in China. CEO Carlos Tavares' leadership is seen as a key factor in navigating these challenges and transforming Stellantis into a sustainable tech mobility company.

feed.title: Thieves cover Union Pacific Railroad train tracks in Los Angeles with stolen cargo and packages, interrupting deliveries
feed.summary: Thieves are targeting Union Pacific freight trains in Los Angeles, breaking into containers and leaving stolen cargo and packages strewn across the tracks. This organized theft operation results in significant litter and interrupted deliveries. Police have increased patrols and are exploring new technologies to combat the ongoing issue.

feed.title: Netflix raises monthly subscription prices in U.S., Canada
feed.summary: Netflix has increased its monthly subscription prices in the U.S. and Canada by $1 to $2, depending on the plan, to fund new programming and maintain competitiveness in the streaming market. The standard U.S. plan now costs $15.49, up from $13.99, while the Canadian standard plan rose to C$16.49 from C$14.99. These increases, the first since October 2020 in these markets, reflect Netflix's pricing power as it faces growing competition from other major streaming services.

feed.title: Renovations to Give Shopping Center New Stores, New Look
feed.summary: The Huntington Shopping Center is undergoing a $75 million renovation by Federal Realty, which will bring new stores, including a Whole Foods Market, outdoor seating, and new entrances. The project, expected to be completed in 2024, will update facades, reconstruct parking lots, and add new landscaping. Long-standing tenants like PetSmart and ULTA will remain, while BuyBuy Baby, Five Guys, and Applebee’s are departing.

feed.title: Costco named MMR Retailer of the Year
feed.summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has been named MMR’s Retailer of the Year for its efficient business model, strong financial performance, and ability to provide an enjoyable shopping experience despite challenges. The company reported significant sales and net income increases in fiscal 2021 and the first quarter of fiscal 2022, driven by its limited product selection, operating efficiencies, and expansion efforts. Costco's Kirkland Signature brand and growing e-commerce presence also contributed to its strong growth and profitability.

feed.title: Train derails near LA site of recent wave of cargo thefts
feed.summary: A train derailed near Los Angeles, close to an area known for recent cargo thefts, leaving 17 cars off the tracks with no reported injuries. Union Pacific is investigating the cause, with some speculation that the derailment could be linked to debris left by thieves who have been targeting cargo containers from major retailers. The railroad has increased patrols and is working with law enforcement to combat the surge in cargo thefts.

feed.title: Federal Realty Maps Out Huntington Retail Redevelopment
feed.summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust is undertaking a $75-million redevelopment of the Huntington Shopping Center in Huntington Station, NY. The project will include significant aesthetic and structural updates, such as new facades, reconstructed parking, landscaping, and outdoor seating. A key part of the redevelopment is the addition of a Whole Foods, aiming to reinvigorate the center and provide essential retail services to the community.

feed.title: Put Disruption By Your Side With GTEK
feed.summary: The article discusses how disruption is a constant force in various industries, regardless of Federal Reserve interest rate actions. It highlights the Goldman Sachs Future Tech Leaders Equity ETF (GTEK) as a means for investors to access these disruptive themes. GTEK focuses on companies with the potential for significant growth, including those outside of large-cap tech and international markets.

feed.title: Netflix earnings to set the pace for 2022 streaming wars
feed.summary: Netflix is set to report its fourth-quarter earnings this week, which will provide insight into the growth of streaming services in 2022. The company, along with competitors like Disney and Amazon, is investing heavily in new content amid intensifying "streaming wars." Analysts expect Netflix's growth to stabilize in 2022, primarily driven by international markets, as competition for subscribers increases, especially in the U.S.

feed.title: Amazon reimagines in-store shopping with Amazon Style
feed.summary: Amazon is launching "Amazon Style," its first physical apparel store, aiming to blend online shopping convenience with an in-store experience. The store will use technology like the Amazon Shopping app and fitting room touchscreens to offer personalized recommendations, efficient item delivery to fitting rooms, and a wide selection of apparel, shoes, and accessories. This new concept seeks to provide a seamless shopping journey for customers, maintaining Amazon.com's pricing while allowing for in-person try-ons.

feed.title: Off the Rails in L.A.
feed.summary: The article discusses a surge in package thefts from Union Pacific trains in Los Angeles, attributing the problem to lax prosecutions by L.A. County District Attorney George Gascón. Union Pacific reported a significant increase in thefts, resulting in millions of dollars in losses and potential diversion of rail business from L.A. The company has increased security measures but faces challenges due to the lack of prosecutorial support.

feed.title: Securities Litigation Team Secures Dismissal of Shareholder Class Action Against GoodRx
feed.summary: Latham & Watkins LLP successfully secured the dismissal of a shareholder class action against GoodRx. The court's decision, issued on January 6, 2022, dismissed all claims, establishing a precedent that damages in Section 11 cases are calculated based on stock price rather than alleged value. The case centered on allegations that GoodRx made misleading statements about Amazon's entry into the prescription discount market.

feed.title: Oracle opens data centre to provide cloud services across Africa
feed.summary: Oracle has launched its first data center in South Africa, providing local cloud services across the African continent to better compete with rivals like Microsoft and Amazon. The new data center in Johannesburg is Oracle's 37th "cloud region" globally, with plans to reach 44 this year. This move caters to the increasing demand for faster computing from African banks and telecom firms, despite challenges such as high power prices and frequent outages in South Africa.

feed.title: Amazon makes more big industrial moves in Mesa
feed.summary: Amazon (AMZN) is undertaking at least three new warehouse projects in southeast Mesa, near the Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport. These moves involve millions of dollars in investment, as the e-commerce giant continues to expand its industrial footprint. The article highlights Amazon's ongoing development in the region, referencing other related projects like annexations and new industrial approvals.

feed.title: Entire Market Value Rule Strikes Again in WDTX
feed.summary: A federal magistrate judge recently granted a defendant's motion to exclude an expert's damages theory for violating the entire market value rule in a patent infringement case. The court found that starting royalty calculations with the total revenue of a multi-component product, even with subsequent apportionment, was improper without strong evidence that the patented feature drives consumer demand for the entire product. This ruling emphasizes the importance for patentees to establish a clear royalty base directly attributable to the infringing feature or prove its substantial impact on customer demand.

feed.title: Tomonari Sato: Why I joined Cloudflare and why I’m helping Cloudflare grow in Japan
feed.summary: Tomonari Sato, with 35 years of experience in the IT industry, has joined Cloudflare as Vice-President and Managing Director in Japan to expand its presence and customer base. He believes Cloudflare's solutions are crucial for Japan's digital transformation, aligning with the government's "Cloud By Default" policy. Sato is enthusiastic about contributing to Cloudflare's mission and helping Japanese organizations leverage its global network for security, performance, and cost efficiency.

feed.title: Oracle opens South African cloud region in Johannesburg
feed.summary: Oracle has launched its first cloud region in Africa, located in Johannesburg, South Africa, making it the company's 37th global cloud region. The company aims to expand to 44 cloud regions by the end of 2022, with plans for further expansion in Africa potentially starting next year, focusing on areas like West Africa. This move places Oracle alongside other major cloud providers like Microsoft and AWS, which already have a presence on the continent, as the demand for data center infrastructure in Africa continues to grow significantly.

feed.title: Stellantis Celebrates First Anniversary as it Speeds Transformation to Sustainable Mobility Tech Company
feed.summary: Stellantis marks its first anniversary, reflecting on a year of significant milestones in its transformation into a sustainable mobility tech company. The company launched over 10 new products, committed over €30 billion to electrification and software strategies by 2025, and forged key partnerships with companies like Amazon and LG Energy Solution. CEO Carlos Tavares highlighted the company's commitment to providing clean, connected, affordable, and safe mobility solutions, with a long-term strategic plan set to be unveiled on March 1, 2022.

feed.title: As talent war wages on, Hilton adds continuing education for thousands of employees to its benefits arsenal
feed.summary: Hilton is expanding its employee benefits by adding continuing education opportunities for thousands of its workers. This move follows a trend set by other large corporations like Amazon, as companies continue to compete for talent. Hilton, headquartered in McLean, aims to enhance its benefits arsenal amidst an ongoing talent war.

feed.title: Amazon to open its first in-person clothing store. What we know about the new Amazon Style.
feed.summary: Amazon announced it is opening its first in-person clothing store, "Amazon Style," in Los Angeles, expanding its physical retail presence. The store will feature a unique design with only one of each item on display and leverage the Amazon app for scanning, trying on, and requesting items, aiming to provide a reimagined and convenient shopping experience. This move is seen as an experiment for Amazon to grow its customer base in fashion and learn about shopper behavior.

feed.title: What is HPC-as-a-service and why does it matter?
feed.summary: High Performance Compute-as-a-service (HPCaaS) is emerging as a critical cloud service, offering hardware, software, and expertise to process demanding workloads like big data analytics. This service addresses the challenges companies face with in-house HPC, such as high costs and specialized staffing, by leveraging cloud infrastructure from providers like IBM and Microsoft Azure. While offering benefits like faster technology integration and dynamic management, HPCaaS also presents challenges related to security, licensing costs, and data transfer, though experts believe these will be overcome by continued innovation, with the market projected to reach $17 billion by 2026.

feed.title: Plastics produce underground success of Advanced Drainage Systems in Hilliard
feed.summary: Advanced Drainage Systems (ADS), based in Hilliard, has achieved significant success with its plastic drainage systems, generating $1.9 billion in annual revenue last year. The company specializes in stormwater management systems for commercial, residential, and agricultural purposes, and is a major plastic recycler in the U.S., diverting over 510 million pounds of plastic from landfills annually. ADS actively collaborates with organizations like The Recycling Partnership and contributes to local Hilliard initiatives for environmental stewardship and sustainable stormwater solutions.

feed.title: Tractor Supply to build $119 million distribution center in Maumelle
feed.summary: Tractor Supply Company plans to build a new $119 million distribution center spanning 899,358 square feet on 119 acres in Maumelle, Arkansas. The development, located at Champs Boulevard and Jackie Burnett Drive, will create 450 jobs with an average wage of $18.50 per hour and an annual payroll of approximately $17 million. This project is part of a trend of new distribution centers being established in the area by major companies.

feed.title: Winky Lux’s Natalie Mackey Talks Retail, Paid Social and Launching in Ulta
feed.summary: Winky Lux CEO Natalie Mackey discusses the company's retail strategy, including its expansion into 350 Ulta doors and the opening of a new microstore in Manhattan. She also talks about the challenges of customer acquisition via social media post-iOS privacy update, highlighting a shift towards omnichannel spending and top-of-funnel advertising, with a focus on channels like TikTok and TV commercials. Mackey predicts a big comeback for makeup in 2022.

feed.title: How to Build a Multicloud Kubernetes Cluster in AWS and Azure Step by Step
feed.summary: This article provides a step-by-step guide to building a multicloud Kubernetes cluster spanning AWS and Azure. It details the process of configuring a master node on AWS and worker nodes across both AWS and Azure, emphasizing the benefits of multicloud deployments like reduced vendor lock-in and increased resilience. The guide also covers troubleshooting and

feed.title: FedEx and Microsoft announce new cross-platform logistics solution for e-commerce
feed.summary: FedEx and Microsoft are expanding their collaboration to introduce a new cross-platform "logistics as a service" solution for retailers, merchants, and brands. This offering will integrate FedEx network intelligence with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management to improve customer engagement, shipping options, and supply chain visibility. The initiative aims to help businesses better fulfill, ship, and service customer orders by leveraging AI and machine learning from the vast data generated by FedEx's daily operations.

feed.title: Peloton’s big whoops
feed.summary: Peloton, which saw a massive surge in demand during the pandemic, is now facing significant challenges, including a demand-supply mismatch and financial struggles. The company is halting production, considering layoffs, and its stock market valuation has dropped considerably from its peak. This situation highlights how difficult it has been for businesses to accurately forecast long-term consumer behavior during uncertain times.

feed.title: Kohl's Possible Sale: Department store chain, target of activist investors, gets a $9 billion buyout offer
feed.summary: Kohl's has received an unsolicited $9 billion buyout offer from a consortium backed by activist investor Starboard Value LP, proposing to take the company private at $64 a share. This bid comes amidst mounting pressure from several activist investors who have criticized Kohl's management and strategy, urging for changes or a potential sale. Kohl's stock closed at $46.84 before the offer, highlighting a significant premium.

feed.title: UIP, Churchill Living acquire 300-unit apartment tower across from Amazon HQ2
feed.summary: UIP Companies, Inc. and Churchill Living have acquired The Millennium, a 300-unit apartment community in Arlington, VA, located across from Amazon's HQ2. The companies plan a $9 million renovation of the building, focusing on high-tech and high-end features, and will convert street-level space into new retail and restaurant amenities. This acquisition aims to capitalize on the anticipated demand for housing and services driven by Amazon's growing presence in National Landing.

feed.title: Amazon Has Stopped Paying Some Workers to Quit
feed.summary: Amazon has discontinued its "Pay to Quit" program for some employees after the holiday season. The initiative, also known as "The Offer," provided warehouse workers with up to $5,000 to leave the company. This decision impacts certain employees, highlighting a shift in Amazon's labor management strategies post-peak season.

feed.title: Abigail Disney Directing New Movie Criticizing Treatment of Cast Members
feed.summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of Disney co-founder Roy O. Disney, has co-directed a new film, "The American Dream and Other Fairy Tales," which critically examines economic inequality in the U.S. and Disney's treatment of its cast members. The film highlights the disparity between executive compensation and cast member wages, with Disneyland and Walt Disney World cast members earning significantly less per hour than the combined $80 million earned by CEOs Bob Chapek and Bob Iger last year. While Disney has not yet secured a distributor, the film aims to spark a conversation about a more equitable future.

feed.title: Is chip giant Nvidia going to scrap its $40BN bid for Arm?
authors: Giles Turner and Peter Elstrom and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to abandon its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to fierce regulatory backlash and little progress in securing approvals. Regulators and customers, including the U.S. FTC, have expressed concerns that the deal would make Nvidia too powerful. SoftBank, Arm's current owner, is stepping up preparations for an Arm initial public offering as an alternative.

feed.title: Webull to Offer Cboe’s Nanos S&P 500 Index Options to Its Retail Traders
feed.summary: Webull Financial LLC announced it will offer Cboe's new Nanos S&P 500 Index options on its trading platform in Q1 2022, expanding its existing offerings of S&P 500 Index (SPX), Mini-S&P 500 Index (XSP), and Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) options. This initiative aims to serve retail traders with more cost-effective and simpler options trading, tailored to varying investment objectives and experience levels. Webull will also provide free subscriptions to Cboe Streaming Market Indices for real-time tracking of SPX, XSP, and VIX index values.

feed.title: Netflix: Why the world's biggest streaming service is frustrated with India
feed.summary: Netflix, despite its global success, is struggling to gain significant traction in the competitive Indian streaming market. With 5.5 million subscribers, it lags far behind rivals like Disney+ Hotstar and Amazon Prime Video, which have focused on local content, sports, and bundled services. Experts suggest Netflix needs to localize its content more deeply and move beyond its "international playbook" to attract a wider Indian audience.

feed.title: GM intends to hire 8,000 for new tech jobs in 2022
feed.summary: General Motors announced plans to hire over 8,000 new technology employees in 2022 to further develop its platform technology and transform into a tech company that also manufactures vehicles. The company's "work appropriately" strategy, allowing flexible work options, has been key in attracting talent, enabling GM to compete with and even recruit from big tech firms. This hiring spree is part of a broader industry trend, with competitors like Ford and Stellantis also investing heavily in expanding their software engineering capabilities.

feed.title: Warehouse Giant Prologis to Offer More Peripheral Services, CFO Says
feed.summary: Prologis Inc., a warehouse giant, plans to expand its revenue streams by offering more peripheral services beyond its core rental income. The company, which currently derives 84% of its revenue from warehouse rentals, aims to provide additional services like solar power, forklifts, and logistics technology. This strategy comes amid strong demand driven by ongoing supply-chain strains and a desire to prepare for future crises.

feed.title: Revolving Door Roundup: Havas Media Group, Joan, Shadow and More
feed.summary: This article summarizes recent noteworthy developments in the advertising and marketing agency world. It details new partnerships, rebrands, and agency launches, including Havas Media Group becoming Edgewell's media agency of record, Joan being selected by S&P Global, and Dolphin Entertainment creating a new Web3-focused agency. The roundup also highlights marketing campaigns featuring celebrity endorsements and innovative technological activations.

feed.title: Kohl's initiated media agency review before buyout offers: Adweek
feed.summary: Kohl’s Corp. initiated a review of its advertising media account before it received any buyout offers. This information comes from Adweek and it suggests that a change in management might render the review moot if the company is sold.

feed.title: Kornit Digital inaugurates Kiryat Gat ink factory
feed.summary: Kornit Digital has opened a new $25 million ink manufacturing factory in Kiryat Gat, Israel, after three years of construction. This facility, spanning 11 dunams, aims to increase production capacity, meet growing global demand, and improve productivity for the next decade. The company views this as a crucial step towards becoming a $1 billion company by 2026 and supporting the textile industry's shift towards sustainability.

feed.title: DISH Sets Data in Motion with Confluent, Unlocking the Power of the First 5G Smart Network™
feed.summary: DISH Network Corporation is partnering with Confluent to leverage cloud-native data streaming with Apache Kafka for real-time analytics on its new smart 5G network. This collaboration, using AWS infrastructure, aims to create a central network nervous system, enabling DISH to deploy a scalable and elastic data architecture that enhances performance, streamlines dynamic behaviors, and provides game-changing real-time intelligence for DISH and its enterprise customers.

feed.title: eBay Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
feed.summary: eBay Inc. (EBAY) stock fell by 1.75% on Thursday, closing at $56.70. This decline occurred during a generally poor trading session for the market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also seeing decreases. The stock underperformed compared to some competitors and closed significantly below its 52-week high.

feed.title: 11 Undervalued Mega-Cap Stocks to Consider
feed.summary: This article identifies 11 undervalued mega-cap stocks that investors should consider, defining mega-caps as companies with market capitalizations over $200 billion. It highlights that the recent market downturn has brought many such stocks into buying range, including detailed analysis for Alphabet, Amazon.com, and AT&T.

feed.title: 3 reasons why Amazon should spend billions to buy Kohl's: analyst
feed.summary: Guggenheim retail analyst Robert Drbul suggests Amazon could acquire Kohl's for three reasons: access to Kohl's customers, expansion of categories like apparel, and leveraging Kohl's store locations. While an offer from Amazon isn't imminent, Kohl's is currently receiving takeover bids from other parties, including a $9 billion offer from Starboard Value. The department store chain is facing pressure from activist investors to improve shareholder value.

feed.title: Framingham grocery store proposal moves another step closer to approval
feed.summary: A proposed grocery store at Framingham's Shoppers World is moving closer to approval after a follow-up traffic study concluded that any increase in area traffic would be negligible. The project involves demolishing a Barnes & Noble and an Old Navy to build a 38,650-square-foot grocery store and three smaller retail spaces. The Planning Board is expected to vote on the proposal at its next meeting on February 3rd.

feed.title: Reed Hasting Bought $20M Worth Of Netflix Stock On Dip Last Week
feed.summary: Netflix Co-CEO Reed Hastings purchased $20 million worth of Netflix shares last week following a significant stock price drop after disappointing subscriber growth forecasts. This move mirrors billionaire investor Bill Ackman's recent acquisition of over $1 billion in NFLX stock, both viewing the dip as a buying opportunity. The article highlights the increased volatility, investor concerns over competition, and the company's recent strategic moves like a gaming business acquisition, amidst a broader market correction.

feed.title: XPO Logistics Launches New Flexible Distribution Model for Omnichannel Retail and E-Commerce Customers
feed.summary: XPO Logistics has launched XPO Direct, a new flexible distribution model designed for omnichannel retail and e-commerce customers. This model utilizes shared-space warehouses and last-mile hubs, supported by their comprehensive transportation network, to offer faster and more cost-effective shipment solutions. The company aims to disrupt traditional distribution methods by leveraging its technology, trucks, and workforce at over 100 sites, enabling goods to reach 95% of the U.S. population within two days.

feed.title: Alabama Port Authority announces new inland intermodal facility, CSX intermodal service from Mobile
feed.summary: The Alabama Port Authority is building an inland intermodal container transfer facility in Montgomery, Alabama, to be served by CSX Transportation. This project, which will cost up to $54 million for its first phase, aims to reestablish regular CSX intermodal service at the Port of Mobile and is expected to create over 2,600 jobs and generate significant business revenues. The announcement comes amidst the port authority's opposition to Amtrak's proposed passenger service between New Orleans and Mobile, raising questions among commentators about the timing and necessity of these developments.

feed.title: Sam’s Club rolls out inventory-checking robots chainwide
feed.summary: Sam's Club is deploying robotic inventory-analysis equipment, powered by Brain Corp software, to all nearly 600 U.S. locations. This technology, mounted on existing autonomous floor-cleaning machines, scans shelves for pricing accuracy, stock levels, and item placement, providing real-time inventory reports to store managers. The move aims to improve efficiency and free up associates for member interaction, aligning with retailers' increasing use of automation to address labor challenges.

feed.title: Univision cerró acuerdo con Televisa para una nueva plataforma de streaming
feed.summary: Univision and Televisa have finalized a $4.8 billion merger, creating a new Spanish-language media giant called TelevisaUnivision Inc. This agreement paves the way for a new streaming service, which will feature both free and premium tiers with a wide range of entertainment, sports, and news content. Despite growing competition in the streaming market, Univision aims to leverage its extensive programming library and vast network of broadcast and cable channels to promote the new platform.

feed.title: Amazon and Microsoft led the world in corporate purchases of clean energy in 2021
feed.summary: Amazon and Microsoft were global leaders in corporate clean energy power purchase agreements in 2021, with Amazon holding the top spot for the second consecutive year. Combined, the two tech giants procured 12.4 GW of wind and solar power, contributing significantly to a record-setting year for corporate carbon-free energy deals. Both companies are committed to achieving 100% renewable energy for their operations by 2025, with Microsoft aiming for 24/7 clean energy by 2030.

feed.title: Televisa y Univision se fusionan para lanzar nueva empresa de streaming y competir con Netflix
feed.summary: Televisa and Univision have merged to create TelevisaUnivision, Inc., a new streaming company aimed at becoming the dominant Spanish-language content producer globally. This new venture seeks to compete with major streaming platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video by targeting the "underserved" Hispanic digital market. The new company, with Televisa as the majority shareholder, will offer a vast catalog of content from both media giants, including a free and premium subscription model, expected to launch in 2022.

feed.title: At Clean Energy Summit, EVs and SCE Take Center Stage
feed.summary: At the Bloomberg NEF Summit, Edison International outlined ambitious efforts to accelerate transportation electrification, particularly focusing on electric vehicles (EVs) and their supporting infrastructure. Southern California Edison (SCE) is investing nearly $800 million in programs like Charge Ready to deploy EV chargers and offers rebates for pre-owned EVs, with a significant emphasis on deploying infrastructure in underserved communities. Leaders from the industry, including those from ABB and EVgo, concur that EV adoption, especially by fleet customers, is growing rapidly and requires substantial grid investments to meet future power demands.

feed.title: Income Is The Outcome
feed.summary: The article discusses the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income Fund, an income-oriented fund that uses equity-linked notes (ELNs) and options premiums to generate substantial income for investors. Despite underperforming market benchmarks in total return, its strategy prioritizes income generation and aims to reduce volatility, allowing investors to stay invested in equities in a more defensive manner. The fund's co-portfolio manager, Hamilton Reiner, explains how the use of ELNs converts options premiums into bona fide income and how market volatility influences the income generated.

feed.title: Robots marched on in 2021, with record orders by North American firms
feed.summary: In 2021, North American companies invested over $2 billion in nearly 40,000 robots, setting a new record for robot orders. The deployment of robots expanded beyond the automotive sector into various industries, including metals, food, consumer goods, and e-commerce, driven by labor shortages and increased demand. A new breed of "cobots" is also emerging, designed to work collaboratively with humans on assembly lines, addressing the need for automation in industries previously resistant to it.

feed.title: Amazon discloses stake in self-driving technology company Aurora
feed.summary: Amazon has acquired a 5% stake in Aurora Innovations Inc., a self-driving technology company based in Pittsburgh. This investment expands Amazon's portfolio in autonomous vehicle technology and signals its interest in alternative solutions for its growing delivery fleet. This move follows Amazon's prior investments in electric vehicle companies, further diversifying its transportation strategy.

feed.title: WD_Black SN770 Gen 4 SSD Review – Don’t Let Its Good Looks Fool You.
feed.summary: This review introduces the WD_Black SN770, a new PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD designed for gaming, available in capacities up to 2TB. Despite being a DRAM-less and single-sided design, it achieves impressive read/write speeds of up to 5GB/s and features a Host Memory Buffer (HMB) to utilize system DRAM. The SN770 targets value and performance for modern users, potentially surpassing more expensive gaming SSDs.

feed.title: The Warm Florida Sun Is Not Helping Dan Loeb
feed.summary: Dan Loeb's Third Point hedge funds experienced significant losses in January, with the Offshore fund declining 7.6% and the Ultra fund slumping 10%, erasing a portion of their previous year's gains. These losses are partly attributed to the poor performance of some top holdings like SentinelOne Inc, Danaher Corp., and Amazon.com Inc. Despite the setback, Third Point and other activist hedge funds, including Elliott Management and Trian Fund Management, are actively engaging in campaigns in the U.K. market, which is seen as ripe for activism due to its size and relatively cheap valuations.

feed.title: Alphabet brings big stock splits back to market
authors: Jeran Wittenstein and Vivianne Rodrigues and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc. announced a 20-for-1 stock split, aiming to make its shares more accessible to small investors by reducing the per-share price. This move is also seen as a step towards potential inclusion in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which has historically been a barrier due to Alphabet's high stock price. The announcement led to a 10% jump in shares during premarket trading.

feed.title: Amazon to Raise Price of Prime Membership
feed.summary: Amazon announced it will increase the price of its annual Prime membership by $20 to $139, and monthly memberships by $2 to $14.99. This is the first price hike in four years, attributed to significant investments in entertainment offerings, including exclusive NFL streaming rights, and an expansion of other Prime benefits. The company also reported strong Q4 2021 earnings, with net sales of $137.4 billion and net income of $14.3 billion.

feed.title: Document
feed.summary: Amazon.com, Inc. announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2021, showing increased net sales but decreased operating cash flow due to higher costs. The company reported a significant net income increase in Q4 2021, boosted by a valuation gain from its investment in Rivian Automotive. Amazon also highlighted continued investments in Prime benefits, expansion of AWS services, and initiatives in environmental protection and community support.

feed.title: Amazon raises Prime membership fees to offset growing costs
feed.summary: Amazon announced it is increasing its Prime membership fees in the United States to offset rising shipping costs and wages, despite exceeding profit expectations for the holiday quarter. The annual membership fee will go up to $139 from $119, effective February 18 for new members. The company's shares saw a significant rise following the announcement, although it also forecast first-quarter sales below Wall Street estimates.

feed.title: Best Buy Selects AWS as Its Strategic Cloud Provider
feed.summary: Best Buy has chosen Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred cloud provider and strategic partner for cloud infrastructure and developing cloud engineering talent. This collaboration aims to enhance Best Buy's use of cloud technology across its retail operations, support rapid innovation in customer experiences, and provide development opportunities for its technology teams. AWS's services will help Best Buy accelerate its cloud migration and implement its cloud-first strategy, while also offering comprehensive cloud training to its employees.

feed.title: Ball Corporation and Anheuser-Busch to Bring Infinitely Recyclable Aluminum Cups to Fans at the Big Game for the Third Consecutive Year
feed.summary: Ball Corporation and Anheuser-Busch are partnering for the third consecutive year to bring infinitely recyclable Ball Aluminum Cups to the Big Game at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on February 13, 2022. This initiative supports both companies' commitments to sustainability, offering a more sustainable packaging solution while educating fans on recycling. The aluminum cups will be available in various sizes at the event and for purchase online and at major retailers.

feed.title: Best Buy in new partnership with Amazon's cloud computing division
feed.summary: Best Buy has partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to accelerate its cloud migration and enhance customer experiences. This collaboration will see Best Buy leveraging AWS's cloud services for various retail operations, including virtual demos and its existing 24/7 chatbot, and investing in cloud engineering talent development. Best Buy aims to move more workloads from on-premises data centers to AWS and expand its use of AWS capabilities and marketplace.

feed.title: This Columbia jacket warms with NASA-inspired technology—and it works wonderfully
feed.summary: This article reviews the Columbia Labyrinth Loop Omni-Heat Infinity Insulated Hooded Jacket, highlighting its "NASA-inspired" Omni-Heat Infinity technology. Lab and wear tests confirm its superior heat retention compared to unlined puffers, even when wet. The jacket is praised for its warmth, comfort, sturdy construction, and style, making it a recommended investment for those in colder climates despite minor storage limitations.

feed.title: Transformers Kingdom Autobot Ark & Teletraan 1 Concept Art by Ken Christiansen
feed.summary: Ken Christiansen has revealed new concept art for the Transformers Kingdom series, specifically featuring the Autobot Ark and Teletraan 1. The designs, including the Ark's bot mode and Teletraan 1 concept, involved collaboration with Takara and Hasbro. These concept drawings offer insight into the development of the figures for collectors.
