feed.title: Sonos Roam tips: how to stereo pair, TV and surround sound support, and more
feed.summary: This article provides comprehensive tips for getting the most out of the Sonos Roam portable speaker, covering its features, capabilities, and limitations. It explains how to stereo pair the Roam, its compatibility with TV and surround sound systems, and other functionalities like Trueplay and hi-res music streaming. The piece also contrasts the Roam with the Sonos Move and guides potential buyers on whether the Roam is the right choice for their needs within the Sonos ecosystem.

feed.title: International Funds Stop Fresh Transactions. Is It a Worrying Sign?
feed.summary: Mutual fund investors were surprised when fund houses stopped fresh transactions in schemes offering exposure to offshore equities. This industry-wide decision was prompted by the Indian mutual fund industry reaching its overall investment limit of USD 7 billion in offshore securities, set by the RBI in 2008. While many funds have temporarily suspended inflows into schemes with overseas exposure, certain overseas ETFs may still accept investments as they fall under a separate, unbreached limit.

feed.title: Weis joins crowded supermarket space in Warminster area. How grocers survive with so many options
feed.summary: Weis Markets recently opened a new 46,000-square-foot store in Warminster, Pennsylvania, entering a highly competitive grocery market. The area already hosts numerous large retailers, and the new store faces challenges common to the industry, such as labor shortages and supply chain disruptions exacerbated by the pandemic. Despite these hurdles, Weis aims to differentiate itself with convenience, value, and community involvement in its expansion efforts in the Philadelphia area.

feed.title: Amazon notches up sunny sales, despite client shift to 'multicloud',
feed.summary: Amazon's cloud computing division, Amazon Web Services (AWS), has continued to show strong sales growth for four consecutive quarters, easing concerns that a move towards "multicloud" strategies by clients would diminish its market share. While some companies are adopting multiple cloud vendors for diversification, major players like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud are still gaining market share from smaller competitors, indicating that even in a multicloud approach, a primary cloud provider often remains dominant. This robust performance underscores significant growth in the wider cloud industry, with overall spending jumping by 37% in 2021.

feed.title: Amazon set for historic market cap gain after Meta’s epic loss
feed.summary: Amazon is projected to add approximately $155 billion in market value if its stock's 11% pre-market gain holds, placing it among the top five single-day gains in U.S. stock market history. This surge follows strong performance in its cloud computing division and a price increase for Amazon Prime, counteracting fears sparked by Meta Platforms Inc.'s recent significant market cap loss. Amazon's expected gain comes after it experienced its own decline, losing $119 billion in market value the day prior due to Meta's earnings flop.

feed.title: Anghami officially lists on US NASDAQ
feed.summary: Music streaming platform Anghami has completed its business combination with Vistas Media Acquisition Company and is now listed on NASDAQ under the tickers "ANGH" and "ANGHW". This marks the first time a regional tech startup has listed on NASDAQ, an achievement highlighted by its co-founders as a significant moment for the Arab world and a step towards expanding Arabic-language music globally. Anghami has also been strengthening its business through significant partnerships and initiatives, including launching a new record label, enhancing interactive experiences with Amazon Alexa, appointing a new Chief Operating and Strategy Officer, and developing innovative entertainment venues and live radio features.

feed.title: Amazon share price surges 19% in post-market trading as company announces price hike in Prime membership
feed.summary: Amazon's stock surged 19% in post-market trading after the e-commerce giant reported better-than-expected profits and announced an increase in its Prime membership price. This rise, along with strong earnings from Snap and Pinterest, helped to alleviate concerns following Meta Platforms' significant stock crash. Despite the after-hours rebound, Amazon and Snap shares only returned to mid-January levels, highlighting the extent of a recent selloff.

feed.title: Why Buying STX Could Be Essential for Lionsgate’s Future
feed.summary: Lionsgate, after a strong 2019, has faced challenges during the pandemic and is exploring selling Starz while considering acquiring STX Entertainment. The potential acquisition of STX would bolster Lionsgate's film library, which is crucial for increasing film licensing revenue, especially if Starz is not sold and the company needs to cover expenses for keeping streaming rights in-house. This move could position Lionsgate as a strong content seller in the competitive streaming landscape.

feed.title: Virtusa and Pegasystems at the service of global insurance
feed.summary: Virtusa, a global IT services company, and Pegasystems, a software company, are collaborating to help the insurance industry embrace digital transformation. The article highlights how this partnership assists insurers in adopting hyper-automation, leveraging low-code/no-code DPA platforms, and modernizing legacy systems to improve efficiency and customer experience. Virtusa's unique approach as a digital engineering company, combined with its long-standing relationship with Pega, positions it to address the insurance sector's evolving needs, especially in a post-pandemic landscape requiring seamless digital interactions.

feed.title: Meta rivalry with Apple inflamed as Facebook parent company share price plummets
feed.summary: Meta's stock price plummeted by 26%, wiping out approximately $220bn in market value, primarily due to "headwinds" caused by Apple's new iOS privacy changes. Mark Zuckerberg blamed these changes, which restrict advertisers' ability to target ads, estimating a $10bn impact on Meta's business. In contrast, other tech companies like Snap, Amazon, and Pinterest reported strong ad revenue or stock growth, indicating that Apple's privacy updates did not affect all companies equally.

feed.title: Dreaming of a Cloud couch? Albany Park's modular, easy-to-assemble couches are luxurious and reasonably priced.
feed.summary: The article highlights Albany Park's Kova sofa collection as a luxurious yet reasonably priced alternative to the popular Restoration Hardware Cloud Sofa. Founded by former NFL linebacker Darryl Sharpton and his wife, Jessica, Albany Park offers modular, easy-to-assemble couches with fast shipping, building on Sharpton's past experience in furniture sales. The direct-to-consumer brand aims to simplify the sofa buying process by focusing on best-selling designs and addressing common customer frustrations.

feed.title: America’s iconic wings concept, ‘It’s Just Wings’, now available through delivery partners in India
feed.summary: Stellar Concepts Pvt. Ltd has launched "It's Just Wings," an American wings concept from Brinker International, in India. The brand offers bone-in and boneless wings with various flavors, sauces, and rubs, exclusively through delivery platforms like Zomato and Swiggy. It aims to cater to the demand for convenient and affordable wing options in cities like Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Delhi-NCR, and Kolkata.

feed.title: Traditional conglomerates such as GE, J&J and Toshiba are moving in a new direction
feed.summary: Traditional conglomerates like General Electric, Johnson & Johnson, and Toshiba are breaking up their companies to increase shareholder value and simplify management. This trend is driven by past financial difficulties and the complexities of their diversified operations. In contrast, modern tech giants like Amazon and Meta thrive as conglomerates by leveraging platform-based models and network effects, which offer a different approach to managing varied businesses.

feed.title: Opinion: $1.4 trillion? Big Tech’s pandemic year produces mind-boggling financial results
feed.summary: In 2021, despite supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, and rising prices, major tech companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft achieved staggering financial results. They collectively saw over $320 billion in profit on $1.4 trillion in sales, with profits increasing more than 55% and sales growing 27% from an already record-setting base. This performance highlights Big Tech's resilience and expanding economic influence, making their combined sales comparable to a top-15 global economy.

feed.title: Why Digital Turbine Stock Plummeted 27.6% in January and Continues to Fall
feed.summary: Digital Turbine (APPS) stock fell 27.6% in January due to a broader market pullback driven by geopolitical tensions, rising interest rates, and inflation. The company's stock continued to decline into February, influenced by mixed Big Tech earnings, although its own third-quarter earnings report is pending. These macroeconomic factors made investors more cautious about growth-dependent tech stocks, impacting Digital Turbine significantly after prior gains.

feed.title: Amazon hiking base salary cap to $350,000 for corporate, tech workers
feed.summary: Amazon has announced a significant increase in its base salary cap for corporate and tech workers, raising it from $160,000 to $350,000. This move aims to enhance the company's competitiveness in a challenging labor market and attract and retain top talent. The company indicated that these increases are "much more considerable" than in previous years, aligning its pay structure more closely with other major tech firms.

feed.title: Fiserv Acquiring Finxact for Digital Banking Acceleration
feed.summary: Fiserv, a payments and financial services platform, has agreed to acquire cloud-native banking solution Finxact Inc. for approximately $650 million. This acquisition aims to accelerate the delivery of digital banking experiences for Fiserv's clients by integrating Finxact's API-first capabilities with Fiserv's existing digital financial solutions. The deal will enable Fiserv to provide a streamlined path for clients to offer advanced digital solutions to their customers.

feed.title: Amazon Is Raising Base Salary Cap to $350,000 From $160,000
feed.summary: Amazon is significantly increasing its maximum base salary for employees from $160,000 to $350,000. This decision comes in response to a highly competitive labor market, aiming to attract and retain top talent. The company cited the need to remain competitive and made substantial adjustments to its compensation levels.

feed.title: Aussie funds exposed to the Meta rout: Charts of the Week
feed.summary: Australian managed funds and popular index-tracking ETFs, including those from Magellan, Hyperion, and Lakehouse, were significantly impacted by Meta Platforms' sharp 26% stock drop, the largest one-day market capitalization loss in US history. This "Meta rout" contributed to new year woes for growth investors, although some losses were mitigated by strong performance from Amazon.com positions within several of these funds. Sustainable funds generally avoided the Meta selloff due to ESG-related exclusions stemming from privacy concerns.

feed.title: Sensor Maker Velodyne Lidar’s Shares Surge After Amazon Investment
feed.summary: Velodyne Lidar Inc.'s stock surged over 50% in after-hours trading following an investment announcement from Amazon. Amazon.com Inc. was issued a warrant to purchase nearly 40 million shares of Velodyne, a maker of sensors for autonomous vehicles. As part of the agreement, Amazon will also gain a board observer position as long as its stake remains above approximately 12.3 million shares.

feed.title: Velodyne Stock Soars After Issuing Warrant to Amazon to Purchase Shares
feed.summary: Velodyne Lidar shares surged after Amazon.com announced it was taking a stake in the company. Investors are now questioning Amazon's interest in the lidar maker.

feed.title: MySize Acquires Orgad, an Omnichannel E-Commerce Platform with a Presence on Amazon.com
feed.summary: MySize, Inc. has acquired Orgad, an omnichannel e-commerce platform with global operations, including on Amazon.com. This strategic acquisition expands MySize's business into direct e-commerce selling and is expected to leverage MySizeID technology to increase profitability by reducing returns. Orgad generated approximately $2.5 million in revenue in 2021 and manages over 1,000 SKUs, primarily in fashion and apparel.

feed.title: Amazon expanding healthcare service to 20 more cities, lands Silicon Labs, Whole Foods Market as customers
feed.summary: Amazon is expanding its healthcare service, Amazon Care, to over 20 additional cities in 2022 and has signed Silicon Labs, TrueBlue, and its own Whole Foods Market as new customers, joining existing clients like Hilton. The virtual health services are now available nationwide, building on a pilot program launched in Seattle in 2019. Amazon Care aims to differentiate itself through on-demand access to high-quality clinicians and a seamless patient experience, addressing a perceived lack of patient-centricity in the traditional healthcare system.

feed.title: Amazon in Pact for Potential Stake in Sensor Maker Velodyne
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. has acquired warrants that could lead to a significant stake in Velodyne Lidar Inc., an auto-sensor maker, causing Velodyne's shares to more than double. This move follows Amazon's pattern of investing in business partners, previously seen with Air Transport Services Group Inc. and Rivian Automotive Inc. Velodyne, a key player in autonomous vehicle technology, previously went public via a SPAC merger but had seen its stock decline significantly.

feed.title: Amazon.com to create 400 jobs in Kenosha with another building lease
feed.summary: Amazon.com is expanding its presence in Kenosha, Wisconsin, by leasing a new 1 million-square-foot distribution center. This expansion is expected to create 400 new jobs in the area. The facility is being developed by Venture One Real Estate.

feed.title: Axon Announces New European R&D Office in London
feed.summary: Axon, a global leader in public safety technologies, has announced the opening of its first European research and development (R&D) office in London. This expansion aims to further Axon's mission to protect life and deliver disruptive technologies to public safety worldwide. Ran Mokady has been appointed as the site lead and Senior Vice President of Real-Time Operations, bringing extensive experience in leading product, design, and engineering teams from companies like Microsoft and Amazon.

feed.title: Peloton hits reset with CEO change, job cuts
feed.summary: Peloton announced a leadership change and job cuts in an effort to revitalize sales and boost investor confidence. Co-founder John Foley will step down as CEO, replaced by former Spotify and Netflix CFO Barry McCarthy, while approximately 2,800 jobs will be eliminated. These moves come after significant stock declines and pressure from activist investor Blackwells Capital, despite which Blackwells remains unconvinced by Foley's continued executive chair role.

feed.title: Discovery, WarnerMedia win Justice Department clearance for merger
feed.summary: The Justice Department has cleared Discovery Inc.'s $43-billion acquisition of WarnerMedia, moving the merger closer to completion. The deal, which will create the new entity Warner Bros. Discovery, is expected to close in April or May, pending Discovery shareholder approval. This merger comes as traditional media companies face challenges from declining ratings and the rise of streaming services.

feed.title: We should never have sold Arm in the first place, says ALEX BRUMMER
feed.summary: Alex Brummer argues that the 2016 sale of British chip designer Arm Holdings to Japan's Softbank for £23 billion was a "serious betrayal" of British technology. He criticizes former Prime Minister Theresa May's government and Cabinet Secretary Jeremy Heywood for facilitating the deal, which he views as short-sighted given Softbank founder Masayoshi Son's intent to use Arm as a bargaining chip rather than for long-term investment. Brummer suggests that following the collapse of Nvidia's £50 billion bid for Arm, the British government has an opportunity to correct past mistakes and bring Arm back to the UK as a public company.

feed.title: Corporate lobbying ETF seeks to profit from influencing politicians
feed.summary: Strategas Asset Management has launched a new exchange-traded fund (ETF), the Strategas Global Policy Opportunities ETF (SAGP-A), designed to invest in companies that demonstrate a strong return on their lobbying efforts in the U.S. federal government. The ETF aims to capitalize on corporate lobbying as a means for companies to gain an earnings advantage, especially in a politically volatile environment. While the existing portfolio has underperformed in recent years, the new ETF includes small and mid-cap companies and non-U.S. firms, which are believed to achieve better returns on lobbying spend, despite some ethical concerns raised by analysts.

feed.title: The Most Durable Baby Wipes for Everyday Mess Management
feed.summary: This article identifies and reviews ten of the most durable and effective baby wipes available, emphasizing their versatility beyond just diaper changes. It highlights key considerations for parents, such as durability, size, ingredients (scented vs. unscented), and environmental impact, including options for compostable and reusable wipes. The selections range from essential oil infused to water-based, catering to various needs and skin sensitivities.

feed.title: KT adds Amazon's Alexa voice service on its AI speakers
feed.summary: South Korean telecom giant KT Corp. has launched a new "Dual Brain AI" service that integrates Amazon's Alexa voice assistant into its GiGA Genie artificial intelligence speakers. This collaboration aims to meet the demand for English education by providing both Korean and English language support, offering access to global content and digital audiobooks. The service is immediately available on 3.1 million GiGa Genie 3 devices, with plans to expand to GiGa Genie 1 and 2 devices by July.

feed.title: What Would It Take for Peloton to Keep Being Peloton?
feed.summary: Peloton faces significant challenges in maintaining its independence amidst declining stock value and increased competition. Following the resignation of CEO John Foley, the company needs to adjust its cost structure, generate more cash, and expand beyond its current product line to avoid acquisition by larger tech companies like Amazon or Apple. Experts suggest Peloton must innovate and build a unique "moat" to sustain its business in a rapidly changing consumer behavior landscape.

feed.title: Is Qualcomm’s New ‘aptX Lossless’ Technology The Holy Grail of Bluetooth?
feed.summary: Qualcomm has announced 'aptX Lossless,' a new capability within its aptX Adaptive codec, designed to deliver true CD-quality (16-bit, 44.1kHz) lossless audio over Bluetooth. This technology aims to overcome the traditional lossy compression of Bluetooth by optimizing wireless connectivity and audio technologies to scale up to approximately 1Mbps for lossless transfer. This development could be a significant step for audiophiles and addresses the growing consumer demand for higher quality streaming audio, allowing the clear transmission of lossless source content from services like Amazon HD.

feed.title: Telkom Kembali Jadi Satu-satunya Perusahaan Indonesia yang Masuk Jajaran Brand Finance Global 500
feed.summary: Telkom Indonesia has once again been recognized as the only Indonesian company to be included in the Brand Finance Global 500 Most Valuable Brand list for 2022, marking its fifth entry. With a brand value of US$4.69 billion, Telkom ranked 490, ahead of many international brands, highlighting the success of its digital transformation strategy. The company also received the award for Indonesia's Most Valuable Brand 2021, credited to its strong brand rating and robust financial performance in Q3 2021.

feed.title: Can A Vintage T. Rowe Price Fund Ride Rivian, Microsoft And Snap To The Moon?
feed.summary: Portfolio manager Joe Fath is revitalizing the T. Rowe Price Growth Stock Fund, founded in 1950, by investing heavily in new tech companies and focusing on "disruptive change," contrasting with the fund's historical picks like IBM. Despite facing outflows to passive management, Fath's strategy involves concentrated bets in private companies like Rivian, and public tech giants such as Microsoft, achieving significant returns. He remains confident in these high-growth, high-volatility investments, believing their long-term growth profiles will ultimately reward shareholders.

feed.title: Two Austin shopping centers with major anchors sell for $189.3 million
feed.summary: InvenTrust Properties Corp. of Illinois has acquired two major shopping centers in South Austin, The Shops at Arbor Trails and Escarpment Village, for a total of $189.3 million. These properties are anchored by significant retailers like Costco, Whole Foods, and H-E-B, highlighting the continued desirability and robust retail market in Austin. The acquisition underscores a strong recovery in the local retail sector, which has seen occupancy rates return to pre-pandemic levels despite challenges in 2020.

feed.title: Knowles Celebrates 75 Years Of Industry Firsts And Leadership In The Audio Industry
feed.summary: Knowles Corporation celebrates 75 years of innovation and leadership in the audio industry, from its founding in 1946 to its current status as a market leader in audio components. The article highlights key milestones such as the development of miniature microphones for hearing aids, the groundbreaking SiSonic MEMS microphones, and balanced armature drivers that have revolutionized both medical and consumer audio. Knowles continues to drive advancements in areas like TWS earphones, voice control, and space exploration, shaping the future of how we interact with sound.

feed.title: Best Load Balancers & Load Balancing Software
feed.summary: This article reviews the best load balancers and load balancing software solutions available, covering a range of types including hardware, software, cloud, and virtual appliances. It details offerings from major vendors like A10 Networks, AWS, Citrix, F5, HAProxy, and VMware, comparing their features, pros, and cons. The piece also explains what load balancing is, how it works, different load balancing algorithms, and what application delivery controllers (ADCs) are, helping readers choose the right solution for their IT infrastructure.

feed.title: Jobs in Hyderabad: Microsoft invites applications from freshers
feed.summary: Microsoft is inviting applications from freshers for engineering jobs in its Hyderabad office. Eligible candidates must have a B.Tech, M.Tech, or MS degree in Computer Science or a related field with a minimum CGPA of 7.5/10 and be from the 2022 batch. Selected candidates may work in Hyderabad, Bangalore, or Noida, with responsibilities including planning, design, and implementation.

feed.title: YPF adopta el sistema «Grab and Go» en sus estaciones de servicio
feed.summary: YPF, in partnership with the startup Intuitivo, has implemented the "Grab and Go" system at its Full service stations in Argentina. This automated shopping method uses QR codes, computer vision, and artificial intelligence, allowing customers to select products without going through a cashier. The initiative is part of YPF's innovation and digitalization efforts to enhance the customer experience.

feed.title: Soros Cut Stake in Big Tech Stocks Before Selloff, Added Peloton
feed.summary: Soros Fund Management significantly reduced its holdings in big tech stocks, including the Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1, Amazon.com Inc., and Alphabet Inc., before the market downturn in January. Concurrently, the investment firm disclosed a new $2 billion stake in electric truck maker Rivian Automotive Inc. and added Peloton.

feed.title: Train Robberies in Los Angeles lead to thousands of missing packages
feed.summary: Thousands of undelivered packages are littering Union Pacific railroad tracks in East Los Angeles due to a surge in train robberies, with a 160 percent increase in criminal rail theft since December 2020. This issue highlights a dispute between Union Pacific, which claims lenient prosecution is to blame, and Los Angeles officials, who cite a decrease in reported cases and an understaffed police force. The widespread thefts have led to calls for increased law enforcement budgets and have focused attention on the vulnerability of the supply chain in Southern California.

feed.title: Billionaire George Soros reveals stake in Rivian, sells some tech shares
feed.summary: Billionaire George Soros' investment fund, Soros Fund Management, acquired a significant stake in electric-pickup maker Rivian Automotive Inc., purchasing nearly 20 million shares worth approximately $2 billion in Q4. This move was disclosed in a recent SEC filing. At the same time, Soros' fund also trimmed positions in major tech companies like Amazon and Alphabet.

feed.title: Manufacturing Acceleration program grants in Western Mass.
feed.summary: Four manufacturers in Western Massachusetts, including Boulevard Machine in Westfield, have received over $556,000 in grants from the Massachusetts Manufacturing Accelerate Program. Boulevard Machine, a SpaceX supplier, will use its $95,838 grant to purchase new tooling equipment to meet demand from the space sector. Other recipients include Advance Welding/Kielb Welding Enterprises, Guardair Corp., and Hi-Tech Mold & Tool, all of whom will use the funding to upgrade equipment and expand operations, contributing to job growth and economic development in the region.

feed.title: TikTok Inks Major Lease in Austin
feed.summary: TikTok has signed a major sublease for over 125,000 square feet at 300 Colorado, a 32-story high-rise in downtown Austin. The social media company will occupy the top six floors of the building, which was completed in 2021. This move comes as the Austin office market experienced significant activity, including a large lease by Meta Platforms, despite overall office vacancy remaining above the city's average.

feed.title: Stanley Druckenmiller Buys Chevron as Family Offices Reveal Stock Picks
feed.summary: Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office sold its Meta Platforms Inc. position and bought Chevron, indicating a shift away from big tech. Similarly, George Soros's family office reduced its stakes in Amazon.com, Alphabet, and a Nasdaq 100 ETF. These moves suggest a trend among some wealthy investors to re-evaluate their portfolios regarding large technology companies.

feed.title: HPE: Storage Management Portfolio Review
feed.summary: This article reviews Hewlett Packard Enterprise's (HPE) storage management portfolio, highlighting its edge-to-cloud products and services. It details various offerings like Data Services Cloud Console, Nimble Storage, and Alletra, alongside HPE's partner program and a successful use case with University Hospital Basel. The report also covers HPE's strong market standing, positive user reviews, and industry recognition in the storage management sector.

feed.title: Oracle adds support for the MongoDB API, makes its case for value of the converged database
feed.summary: Oracle has announced support for the MongoDB API, allowing enterprises to run MongoDB data applications on Oracle Autonomous Database without retooling their MongoDB environment. This move, highlighted by Oracle's Gerald Venzl, signifies a continuation of the converged database strategy, enabling users to leverage both SQL and NoSQL functionalities within a single cloud service. Oracle believes this offers a distinct advantage over competitors by providing a full array of data models and analytics capabilities without requiring multiple services.

feed.title: VF’s Dickies Brand Boosts Conversions, Slashes Returns With Virtual Fitting
feed.summary: VF Corp.'s Dickies brand has significantly increased conversions and customer satisfaction while reducing returns through an AI-driven virtual fitting program implemented less than a year ago. The program, developed with 3DLOOK, uses AI to help online shoppers find the correct size by analyzing photos, and has resulted in a 94% increase in conversions. This initiative highlights a broader trend in retail towards using technology to improve the online shopping experience and address fit issues.

feed.title: Rivian stock surges after George Soros' fund disclosed $2 billion investment
feed.summary: Rivian stock saw a significant surge after news broke that George Soros' fund had disclosed a roughly $2 billion investment in the electric vehicle manufacturer. The investment, revealed via a December 2021 report, contributed to a 12% jump in Rivian shares, although the exact timing and purchase price of the shares remain unknown. This positive sentiment was further bolstered by Amazon's previous investment and contractual agreement with Rivian for 100,000 electric vehicles.

feed.title: Omnicom Scores Big in USA TODAY's 34th Annual Ad Meter Competition for Super Bowl LVI Ads
feed.summary: Omnicom Group Inc. announced that three commercials created by its agencies ranked in the top ten of USA TODAY's 34th annual Ad Meter competition for Super Bowl LVI. Lucky Generals for Amazon and Goodby Silverstein & Partners for Doritos/Cheetos Flamin' Hot secured the #2 and #3 spots respectively, with BMW's "Zeus & Hera" by GS&P ranking #7. This marks a significant achievement for Omnicom agencies, highlighting their creativity and effectiveness in capturing consumer attention during the Super Bowl.

feed.title: WaveDancer Blockchain approved for use on Amazon Web Services (AWS) Marketplace for GovCloud
feed.summary: WaveDancer announced that its supply chain management blockchain platform is now available on Amazon Web Services (AWS) Marketplace for GovCloud. This move allows U.S. Government agencies to access WaveDancer's unique blockchain, AI, and IoT capabilities for secure and scalable supply chain solutions. The company aims to facilitate better management of "big data" and sensitive information for complex global operations.

feed.title: Unpacking the 2022 Construction Outlook with Amazon, Hensel Phelps, Autodesk, and ENR
feed.summary: This article explores the 2022 construction outlook, highlighting six major industry trends and innovative strategies with insights from Amazon, Hensel Phelps, Autodesk, and ENR. Key discussions include the increasing role of prefabrication, jobsite technology, effective new technology implementation, the growing impact of robotics and AI, essential cloud-based construction strategies, and the critical importance of data quality. The experts also reflect on what worked in 2021 to inform future plans.

feed.title: Akamai pays $900M to acquire AWS cloud infrastructure rival Linode
feed.summary: Akamai Technologies Inc. has announced its acquisition of Linode LLC for approximately $900 million. This strategic move aims to transform Akamai into a highly distributed compute platform, enhancing its offerings for developers by combining Linode's cloud computing capabilities with Akamai's edge platform and security tools. The acquisition follows Akamai's strong fourth-quarter financial results and is expected to add about $100 million in revenue by year-end.

feed.title: Amazon, Walmart and JPMorgan Chase among companies relaxing employee mask mandates
feed.summary: Several major U.S. companies, including Amazon, Walmart, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, HSBC, and Wells Fargo, are relaxing their mask mandates for employees, particularly for fully vaccinated staff, unless local regulations state otherwise. This move follows similar decisions by multiple states to drop indoor mask mandates, citing declining COVID-19 cases and increasing vaccination rates. However, some exceptions remain, such as employees in pharmacies, health clinics, and certain branch offices, who may still be required to wear masks.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase spent $2 billion on brand new data centers last year
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase invested $2 billion in new data centers last year, even while actively migrating data and applications to public cloud platforms like AWS, Google, and Microsoft. This investment is part of their broader annual technology spending, which exceeded $12 billion, focusing on cloud capabilities, digital consumer experience, and data analytics. CEO Jamie Dimon emphasized that the new data centers incorporate "cloud capability," and the firm plans to move 30% to 50% of its applications to the cloud this year, driven by the significant value seen in risk management, fraud prevention, and customer satisfaction.

feed.title: What’s new in space
feed.summary: Microchip Technology's senior manager of product marketing, Nicolas Ganry, discusses how the company supports the "New Space" industry by providing components that meet the demanding reliability and cost requirements of new satellite constellations and space missions. Microchip, a leading supplier of commercial space components, focuses on delivering a wide range of qualified products, including radiation-hardened devices and COTS upgrades, to reduce development costs and accelerate time to market. The company partners with various entities, from new space companies to governments and universities, to offer scalable solutions for successful space missions.

feed.title: AWS File Storage with AWS Lambda
feed.summary: This article discusses the integration of AWS file storage solutions with AWS Lambda in serverless architectures. It explores various AWS file storage options like Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, and NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP, highlighting their pros and cons for use with serverless functions. The piece emphasizes the importance of persistent data stores for AWS Lambda functions and details how different storage services cater to specific file sharing and performance requirements.

feed.title: Oracle cloud authorized to host top secret data for DOD
feed.summary: Oracle's cloud technology has received authorization to host top secret and highly sensitive data for the Department of Defense, specifically for the Air Force. The company built special "National Security Regions" to secure this sensitive information. This accreditation positions Oracle alongside Microsoft and Amazon Web Services, which have also been cleared for similar highly sensitive data hosting.

feed.title: Oracle cloud authorized to host top secret data for DOD
feed.summary: Oracle has received authorization to host top secret and sensitive compartmentalized information (TS/SCI) and special access program data for the Department of Defense, specifically the Air Force. The company achieved an Authority to Operate (ATO) for its "National Security Regions" which are designed with robust security features. This accreditation allows Oracle to process some of the Air Force's most sensitive data, joining other major cloud providers like Microsoft and Amazon Web Services in this capability.

feed.title: Grubhub expands convenience channel Grubhub Goods nationwide
feed.summary: Grubhub has announced the nationwide launch of Grubhub Goods, its on-demand convenience channel, expanding its offerings beyond traditional restaurant delivery. This initiative, stemming from a successful pilot with 7-Eleven in Manhattan, allows customers to order convenience store items from over 3,000 locations. The expansion highlights a broader trend among delivery aggregators to diversify services and tap into growing consumer demand for efficient delivery of various product types.

feed.title: KT to join MBK, IMM in Megazone Cloud's $400 mn funding
feed.summary: KT Corp. is investing $110 million in Megazone Cloud Corp., South Korea's largest cloud services provider, as part of a Series C funding round totaling $440 million which also includes investments from MBK Partners and IMM Private Equity. This investment helps Megazone Cloud achieve unicorn status and aims to bolster KT's digital transformation, integrating AI, big data, and cloud computing as core business pillars. The deal is KT's second major startup investment exceeding 100 billion won, signaling a strategic push into the rapidly expanding cloud services market.

feed.title: Oracle gets go-ahead to host top secret Air Force data
feed.summary: Oracle has received authorization to host top-secret U.S. Air Force data on its National Security Regions cloud platforms. This expands Oracle's role in the military sector, allowing it to handle highly sensitive information for the Department of Defense. The company has a history of government contracts, including involvement with the Air Force's Advanced Battle Management System and the CIA's Commercial Cloud Enterprise.

feed.title: CDN company Akamai enters cloud business with $900m Linode acquisition
feed.summary: Akamai Technologies is acquiring cloud hosting company Linode for $900 million, marking Akamai's entry into the cloud business. This acquisition aims to combine Linode's developer-friendly cloud computing with Akamai's edge platform and security services to create a unique cloud platform for building, running, and securing applications from cloud to edge. The deal is expected to create "the world’s most distributed compute platform" and is scheduled to close in late Q1 2022.

feed.title: Mindy Kaling, Amazon Publishing, and Amazon Studios Announce Mindy’s Book Studio and First-Look Deal, a New Home for Dynamic Storytelling
feed.summary: Mindy Kaling is collaborating with Amazon Publishing and Amazon Studios to launch "Mindy’s Book Studio," aimed at publishing diverse voices and adapting their stories for film on Prime Video. Kaling will also publish her debut novel and a new essay collection with Amazon Publishing, with Amazon Studios acquiring first-look rights for adaptations. The initiative seeks to expand Kaling's storytelling impact by bringing a variety of compelling narratives to readers and viewers.

feed.title: Elastic (ESTC) Settles Trademark Lawsuit Against Amazon’s (AMZN) Cloud Unit
feed.summary: Elastic NV has settled a two-year-old trademark lawsuit against Amazon Web Services (AWS) regarding the use of the Elasticsearch name. AWS has agreed to cease using the Elasticsearch name for its projects and services. The settlement terms, beyond the naming agreement, were not disclosed.

feed.title: Tenovos Named a Strong Performer in Digital Asset Management for Customer Experience by Independent Research Firm
feed.summary: Tenovos, a provider of Digital Asset Management (DAM) software, has been recognized as a 'Strong Performer' in The Forrester Wave™: Digital Asset Management for Customer Experience, Q1 2022 report. Despite being only in its third year, Tenovos was lauded for its intelligent content generation capabilities, strong enterprise platform integrations, and focused market approach targeting large B2C and direct-to-consumer brands. The company has seen 100% year-over-year revenue growth due to new client acquisitions like Marvel, Amazon XCM, and Canadian Tire.

feed.title: Radware Acquiring SecurityDAM for $30 Million to Accelerate Cloud Security Services
feed.summary: Radware is acquiring SecurityDAM for $30 million, with potential contingent payments up to $12.5 million, to boost its cloud security services. This acquisition will allow Radware to expand its cloud network footprint, capacity, and service divisions, creating new opportunities for partners and enhancing its competitive product offerings. The initiative includes opening and expanding cloud security centers globally and innovating its cloud security data center architecture to meet growing demand for cloud security services.

feed.title: Walmart posts record holiday sales as spending remains firm
feed.summary: Walmart Inc. reported record holiday season sales, exceeding $150 billion in fourth-quarter revenue for the first time, defying supply chain issues and rising inflation. The company attributed its success to investments in chartering ships, raising worker wages, and sourcing over two-thirds of its products domestically, which helped it maintain competitive pricing, especially in groceries. Walmart forecasts continued sales and earnings gains for 2022, signaling confidence in sustained consumer spending.

feed.title: 3 Lidar Stocks to Buy as Amazon Bet Shines Light on Autonomous Vehicles
feed.summary: The lidar market is poised for significant growth, with the global automotive lidar sensor market projected to reach $2.5 billion by 2026. This article highlights three lidar stocks—Innoviz Technologies (INVZ), Luminar Technologies (LAZR), and Ouster (OUST)—as attractive long-term opportunities due to their innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and current valuation pullbacks. These companies are actively working to establish themselves as key players in the expanding autonomous vehicle and industrial automation sectors.

feed.title: Samsung SDS joins hands with Amazon for global cloud business
feed.summary: Samsung SDS, the IT service arm of Samsung Group, is partnering with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to expand its global cloud service business. By joining AWS's exclusive global business network, Samsung SDS aims to enhance its market presence as a managed service provider (MSP) and offer its software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions on the AWS cloud platform. This collaboration focuses on driving digital transformation and capitalizing on the growing global managed service market, projected to reach $552.4 billion by 2028.

feed.title: After delaying over crime concerns, Weyerhaeuser says workers will return to downtown Seattle office
feed.summary: Weyerhaeuser is set to reopen its Pioneer Square headquarters in April 2022, after delaying reopening efforts last fall due to concerns about street crime in downtown Seattle. The timber company will implement a hybrid work schedule for employees. This move follows similar announcements from Microsoft and Expedia, signaling a broader return to office for Seattle-based companies.

feed.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific and Accenture team on their XR journey and delivering 3D content at scale (podcast)
feed.summary: This article discusses a collaboration between Thermo Fisher Scientific, Accenture, and Amazon Web Services (AWS) to develop a 3D management system for Extended Reality (XR) content. The initiative aims to showcase how 3D content can solve problems and impact XR, addressing common pitfalls in metaverse strategies. The core of the article highlights a podcast featuring key figures from Thermo Fisher Scientific and Accenture discussing their journey in delivering 3D content at scale.

feed.title: Inside the $644 billion business of reselling returned items, from electronics to bizarre finds
feed.summary: The liquidation market, which resells returned goods, has grown into a $644 billion industry due to the increasing volume of returns, particularly from online shopping. This sector offers a solution for retailers facing significant costs and environmental impact from returns, with companies like Liquidity Services and B-Stock Solutions specializing in reselling everything from electronics to unusual items. The boom in liquidation is also fueled by growing consumer demand for sustainable and secondhand goods, leading to the rise of direct-to-consumer liquidation stores and refurbished item marketplaces.

feed.title: Medtronic to provide underserved communities with artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted colonoscopy technology through Health Equity Assistance Program for colon cancer screening
feed.summary: Medtronic, in collaboration with the American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ASGE) and supported by Amazon Web Services (AWS), is launching a Health Equity Assistance Program to provide AI-assisted colonoscopy technology to underserved communities in the U.S. The initiative involves donating 50 Medtronic GI Genius™ intelligent endoscopy modules to facilities that primarily serve communities with low screening rates or limited access to the technology, aiming to improve early detection of colorectal cancer. This effort is part of Medtronic's "Zero Barriers" commitment to reduce health disparities and enhance patient outcomes by expanding access to advanced healthcare technologies.

feed.title: Macy’s Declines to Spin Off Ecommerce Operations, Citing ‘High Execution Risk’
feed.summary: Macy's Board of Directors has decided against spinning off its e-commerce operations into a separate company, despite pressure from activist investor Jana Partners. The decision was based on "high execution risk," significant separation costs, and ongoing operational expenses. Instead, Macy's will continue to integrate its digital business and double down on its Polaris transformation strategy, which has already led to strong financial results exceeding pre-pandemic levels.

feed.title: Yeti to stop selling at Lowe's, part of a wholesale pullback to focus on corporate giving, digital and stores
feed.summary: Yeti Holdings Inc. announced it will cease selling its products at Lowe's Cos. Inc. as part of a broader strategy to reduce its wholesale presence. The company plans to reallocate resources to channels that offer greater business opportunities, including corporate gift-giving, its retail stores, and an enhanced focus on its mobile digital platform. This shift aims to leverage the popularity of Yeti products for corporate gifts and holidays, as well as optimize its burgeoning digital traffic.

feed.title: Tractor Supply Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
feed.summary: Tractor Supply Co. (TSCO) stock declined by 6.45% on Tuesday, closing at $200.36, amidst a broad market downturn. This performance saw the company underperform compared to major market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, and also in relation to some of its competitors such as Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Home Depot Inc. (HD), and Lowe's Cos. (LOW). The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, with trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

feed.title: Target to accept drive-up returns in Twin Cities, other test markets
feed.summary: Target will begin piloting a drive-up return service and allow customers to order Starbucks drinks via drive-up in the Twin Cities and other test markets this fall. This move is part of a broader trend among retailers to innovate their returns processes and enhance the omnichannel shopping experience. The company has also removed its mask mandate for employees and customers in stores unless local rules require otherwise.

feed.title: Warner Music and BlackRock Invest $750 Million in Influence Media, Female-Led Music-Rights Firm
feed.summary: Warner Music Group and BlackRock have jointly invested $750 million in Influence Media, a female-led music-rights firm. This partnership aims to acquire music-rights catalogs from female and diverse artists, focusing on newer, active catalogs rather than established older artists. Influence Media, founded by Lylette Pizarro and Lynn Hazan, plans to work with artists who will retain a stake in their work, and has already invested $300 million in 20 catalogs, including that of songwriter-producer Tainy and hitmaking team The Stereotypes.

feed.title: E-commerce: EBay forecasts bleak quarter as pandemic-driven online demand wanes
feed.summary: EBay Inc. forecasts a challenging first quarter with lower-than-expected profits and revenue due to waning online demand, increased competition, and supply chain issues. The company's shares fell significantly as the pandemic-driven e-commerce boom subsides and consumers return to in-person shopping, mirroring a trend also seen by Amazon. Despite this, eBay's fourth-quarter results exceeded analyst estimates for profit and revenue, though gross merchandise volume and active buyers declined.

feed.title: Grocery Outlet opens Northeast Philadelphia store amid continued local expansion
feed.summary: Grocery Outlet has opened a new store in Northeast Philadelphia, marking its eighth location in the greater Philadelphia area. The grocery chain is known for selling products at a discount of 40% to 50% below brand prices. This expansion is part of its continued local growth in the region.

feed.title: Drug Channels News Roundup, February 2022: Mark Cuban vs. Generics, Novo Nordisk’s G2N, CVS & 340B, and My Favorite Chart
feed.summary: This roundup discusses Mark Cuban's entry into the cash-pay generic drug market, questioning its novelty and competitive edge. It also highlights Novo Nordisk's 2021 financial report showing a significant drop in net drug prices despite a slight list price increase, challenging common perceptions of "skyrocketing" drug costs. Furthermore, the article examines CVS Health's acknowledgment of its 340B program profits, indicating potential reform in the program, and includes an updated economic chart for reflection.

feed.title: For Many Consumers Gift Cards Remain Their Preferred Gift, a Fiserv Survey Says
feed.summary: A Fiserv survey indicates that gift card sales remained steady in 2021, with 73% of consumers purchasing the same or more cards than the previous year. Online merchants, particularly Amazon, were the primary beneficiaries. The study also highlights popular reasons for buying gift cards, consumer preferences for digital versus physical cards, and desired future innovations.

feed.title: Amazon’s India Partner Samara Capital Plans $500 Million Fund
feed.summary: Samara Capital, an India-focused private equity firm and local partner of Amazon.com Inc., is planning to raise up to $500 million for a new fund. The fund will target companies in retail, health care, technology, and finance sectors in India, with plans to close in the second half of 2022. This initiative highlights Samara Capital's continued investment strategy in Asia's third-biggest economy.

feed.title: Walmart’s Continued Advantage Over Amazon? Real Estate
feed.summary: Walmart continues to leverage its extensive real estate footprint as a significant competitive advantage over Amazon, turning its numerous physical stores into fulfillment centers and customer touchpoints. The company's omnichannel strategy, which includes over 4,600 locations for in-store pickup and 3,500 for same-day delivery, allows it to deliver products to customers in hours rather than days. Walmart is also modernizing its stores to create experiential retail environments and generate additional revenue through programs like Walmart Connect, demonstrating its commitment to integrating its physical and online presence.

feed.title: Kroger Porter Five Forces Analysis
feed.summary: This article provides a Porter Five Forces analysis of Kroger, a major multi-department supermarket chain in the United States. It evaluates the threat of new entrants (moderately high), threat of substitutes (high), bargaining power of customers (high), bargaining power of suppliers (very low), and competitive rivalry (high). The analysis highlights the intense competition in the retail market and the factors influencing Kroger's competitive environment.

feed.title: Teladoc telehealth services roll out on Amazon's Alexa
feed.summary: Teladoc Health has launched its telehealth services on Amazon's Alexa, allowing users to connect with a Teladoc care provider through Amazon Echo devices. This collaboration aims to provide a convenient new access point for virtual healthcare consultations. The service rolled out on February 28, 2022, enhancing telehealth accessibility.

feed.title: You can now ask Amazon’s Alexa to call you a doctor
feed.summary: Amazon and Teladoc Health have partnered to launch a voice-activated virtual care program through Alexa. Users of Amazon Echo devices can now request a call back from a Teladoc physician for non-emergency health issues, marking Amazon's continued expansion into the healthcare sector. This initiative aims to provide convenient, round-the-clock medical assistance, initially offering audio-only calls with video capabilities expected soon, and doctors able to prescribe medication in some cases.

feed.title: Amazon, Teladoc Health Makes Basic Healthcare More Convenient And Accessible With New Alexa-Powered Telehealth Calling Feature
feed.summary: Amazon and Teladoc Health have partnered to integrate telehealth services into select Alexa-powered devices, allowing users to access basic healthcare consultations 24/7. This new feature enables individuals to connect with a doctor for non-emergency medical needs, making healthcare more accessible, especially for disabled and immunocompromised individuals. It expands Alexa's utility beyond trivia, demonstrating the potential of virtual assistants in providing practical, life-saving services.

feed.title: Teladoc to partner with Amazon on Alexa-enabled virtual visits
feed.summary: Teladoc Health announced a partnership with Amazon to launch voice-activated virtual care on Alexa-supported Echo devices, allowing U.S. customers to connect with a Teladoc provider via audio for general medical needs. Users can initiate a visit by saying "Alexa, I want to talk to a doctor," with video visits planned for the future. This collaboration expands Amazon's healthcare initiatives and aims to improve access to care.

feed.title: General Dynamics IT President Amy Gilliland Named to 2022 Wash100 Award for Leadership in Cloud Modernization and Cybersecurity Services
feed.summary: Amy Gilliland, president of General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), has been named a 2022 Wash100 Award recipient for her leadership in cloud modernization and cybersecurity services. This marks her fifth consecutive inclusion on the annual list, recognizing her influence and ability to maintain GDIT's stability and growth. Under her leadership, GDIT secured significant contracts, including a $4.5 billion agreement with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and a $190 million contract to migrate the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's IT infrastructure to the cloud.

feed.title: Amazon, General Mills, IBM, Microsoft, and Nestle Join 150+ Major U.S. Companies To Oppose Anti-Transgender Legislation in Iowa
feed.summary: Over 150 major U.S. companies, including Amazon, General Mills, IBM, Microsoft, and Nestle, have publicly opposed anti-LGBTQ+ legislation across the country, particularly targeting transgender youth. Business leaders emphasize that such discriminatory laws negatively impact recruitment, retention, and overall business operations, making it difficult to attract and keep talent. The Human Rights Campaign and Freedom for All Americans highlight that these policies harm employees, customers, and communities, urging lawmakers to abandon discriminatory efforts.

feed.title: Teladoc Health and Amazon Team Up to Launch Teladoc on Alexa
feed.summary: Teladoc Health has partnered with Amazon to launch voice-activated general medical virtual care on supported Echo devices, allowing U.S. customers to connect with a Teladoc care provider 24/7. This integration aims to provide convenient, hands-free access to virtual doctor visits for non-emergency health needs, with video visits to be introduced soon. The service addresses healthcare accessibility barriers by meeting consumers where they are, offering visits potentially as low as $0 with insurance or $75 without.

feed.title: Need a doctor? Alexa can now arrange virtual house calls via Teladoc
feed.summary: Amazon's Alexa can now facilitate virtual doctor visits through a partnership with Teladoc Health. Users can initiate audio-only calls for non-emergency medical needs, with video calls planned for the future. The cost of a Teladoc call via Alexa can vary based on insurance coverage, potentially reaching up to $75 without it.

feed.title: KYNDRYL REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL-YEAR 2021 RESULTS
feed.summary: Kyndryl Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: KD) reported its fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 financial results, with full-year revenues totaling $18.7 billion and a net loss of $2.3 billion. The company is strategically positioning itself for growth through new partnerships with cloud hyperscalers and key initiatives focused on increasing signings, transforming service delivery, and addressing substandard margins. Kyndryl also announced significant strategic partnerships with major cloud providers and an expanded customer base following its spin-off from IBM.

feed.title: Velodyne Lidar Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Financial Results
feed.summary: Velodyne Lidar announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2021, reporting significant sensor unit shipments and revenue growth. The company sold over 4,900 sensor units in Q4 and shipped more than 15,000 sensors in 2021, achieving revenues of $17.5 million and $61.9 million for the respective periods. Velodyne's CEO, Dr. Ted Tewksbury, highlighted strategic pillars for 2022, focusing on market expansion, technological development, and operational excellence, expecting lidar to revolutionize various industries with an estimated total available market of $5.7 billion by 2026.

feed.title: Target Positions Itself as Benefits Leader With Up to $24 Starting Wage
feed.summary: Target is investing $300 million in 2022 to enhance employee benefits, including raising its starting wage range to $15-$24 an hour and expanding access to health care for its team members. This initiative will make about 20% of Target's team newly eligible for comprehensive health care benefits, with reduced waiting periods and expanded wellness offerings. These changes are part of Target's ongoing strategy to create equity and opportunity, building on previous enhancements like debt-free college programs and permanent Thanksgiving Day store closings.

feed.title: Federal Realty Announces Major Overhaul of Huntington Shopping Center in Long Island
feed.summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust is undertaking a $75 million redevelopment of the Huntington Shopping Center in Dix Hills, Long Island. The overhaul includes building a new Whole Foods Market, enhancing parking, installing public seating, and adding new entrances. Construction is expected to finish by the end of 2024, with other tenants remaining open during the process.

feed.title: File your taxes on time with H&R Block Deluxe and State for $33
feed.summary: Amazon is offering H&R Block Tax Software Deluxe + State 2022 for $32.89, a significant discount from its $45 MSRP. This digital download assists with federal and state income tax filing, covers various income streams and deductions, and includes five free federal e-files. While state e-filing costs extra and is not available in New Hampshire, it remains a valuable tool for timely tax preparation.

feed.title: At Snap Inc., Making Augmented Reality Work for Fashion
feed.summary: Snap Inc. is making significant strides in augmented reality (AR) for the fashion industry, with over 200 million Snapchat users engaging with AR daily. Peter Sellis, VP of Product at Snap Inc., discusses how AR technologies, including virtual try-ons and spatial technology, are evolving to enhance shopping experiences, reduce returns, and increase conversions for brands like Prada, Farfetch, and Gucci. The commercial benefits and future product innovations, such as cloth simulation and 3D asset management, are highlighted as key drivers for investment in AR within fashion.

feed.title: Seven Must-Visit Food Halls to Inspire a Gastronomic Getaway
feed.summary: This article highlights seven must-visit food halls across the globe, from Birmingham, Alabama to Tijuana, Mexico, offering diverse culinary experiences for travelers. It emphasizes the growing popularity of food halls as a way to savor local and international cuisine in a relaxed setting, appealing to 51% of global travelers seeking food and drink experiences on their vacations. Each location includes recommendations for local delicacies, additional activities, and nearby hotel stays to inspire gastronomic getaways.

feed.title: Check Point releases 2022 Cloud Security Report
feed.summary: Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. has released its 2022 Cloud Security Report, highlighting the challenges organizations face in securing cloud infrastructures amidst increasing cloud adoption, a cyber-skills shortage, and a rise in cloud security incidents, primarily due to misconfigurations. The report suggests a growing preference for independent cloud security solutions over cloud vendor security to streamline management across multi-cloud environments. TJ Gonen, VP of Cloud Security at Check Point, emphasizes the need for integrated third-party solutions with unified dashboards to simplify cloud security, reduce misconfiguration risks, and support application development in the cloud.

feed.title: Colgate launches $10 ‘premium’ toothpaste
feed.summary: Colgate-Palmolive has launched a new "premium" teeth-whitening toothpaste, Optic White Pro Series, retailing for $10 a tube. This move is part of the company's strategy to raise prices on its products. The launch comes amidst rising inflation, which is squeezing American consumers' finances.

feed.title: 7 E-Commerce Stocks to Buy as Shopify Suffers
feed.summary: Despite a volatile market and a significant drop in high-growth e-commerce stocks like Shopify, the e-commerce industry is projected for substantial growth, with global revenue expected to exceed $7 trillion by 2025. This article identifies seven e-commerce stocks, including Amazon, Etsy, and Target, that offer attractive long-term potential for investors in 2022. Each stock analysis provides financial highlights, market performance, and future outlook, emphasizing their resilience and growth drivers amidst current market headwinds.

feed.title: Amazon Closing All Bookstores, Shops to Focus on Grocery Sector
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. is closing all of its physical bookstores, Amazon 4-Star locations, and mall pop-up kiosks to concentrate its brick-and-mortar efforts on the grocery sector. The company will focus on its Amazon Fresh, Whole Foods Market, Amazon Go, and Amazon Style stores, as well as its Just Walk Out technology. This strategic shift involves the closure of 24 bookstores, 33 Amazon 4-Stars, and nine pop-up kiosks, while Whole Foods Market remains its largest physical presence.

feed.title: Amazon Closing Bookstores and Shops to Focus on Grocery Sector
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. is closing all of its physical bookstores, "Amazon 4-Star" locations, and mall pop-up kiosks to concentrate its brick-and-mortar retail efforts on the grocery sector. The company plans to prioritize Amazon Fresh, Whole Foods Market, Amazon Go, and Amazon Style stores, along with its "Just Walk Out" technology. Amazon stated it remains committed to physical retail experiences and will assist affected employees in finding new roles within the company.

feed.title: Colgate launches $10 ‘premium’ toothpaste
feed.summary: Colgate-Palmolive is launching a new "premium" Optic White Pro Series toothpaste that costs $10 for a 3-ounce tube, featuring 5% hydrogen peroxide to whiten teeth and remove 15 years of stains. This move comes as the company seeks to raise prices amidst rising inflation, following similar price hikes by other major companies like Amazon and Dollar Tree. The introduction of this high-priced product highlights a trend towards premiumization in consumer goods during a period when many Americans are facing financial strain due to inflation.

feed.title: Amazon to close Green Hills store amid nationwide move
feed.summary: Amazon announced it would close 68 physical retail locations, including its Green Hills Amazon Books store in Nashville, as it shifts its focus toward groceries and fashion. Despite the closures, the company stated it is not abandoning brick-and-mortar sales entirely. This move comes as Amazon opened its first Nashville Amazon Books location in The Mall at Green Hills.

feed.title: DigitalOcean vs Cloudflare — which stock can take advantage of cloud expansion?
feed.summary: This article compares DigitalOcean Holdings (DOCN) and Cloudflare (NET), two cloud computing companies, to determine which is the better investment. DigitalOcean serves developers and SMBs, while Cloudflare focuses on web security and content delivery. The analysis concludes that Cloudflare is the less risky and better investment due to its continued large client growth and potential for SMB expansion, despite DigitalOcean's strong performance and hold in the SMB market.

feed.title: Wide Moat Stock Outlook Remains Compelling
feed.summary: The article discusses the compelling outlook for wide moat stocks, highlighting their historical outperformance, especially in rising interest rate and high inflation environments. feed.title: How A Failed Experiment Led To Bubble Wrap
feed.summary: Bubble Wrap, a ubiquitous packaging material, was created accidentally in 1957 by Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes. Their initial attempt to create textured wallpaper resulted in air bubbles trapped between plastic sheets. After failing to market it as insulation, they founded Sealed Air Corp. in 1960, and their product found its true purpose protecting delicate equipment for IBM, leading to its widespread adoption and the company's success.

feed.title: How Hyperscale Data Centers are reshaping India’s IT
feed.summary: Hyperscale data centers are critical infrastructure for companies like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, providing dedicated computing resources to handle massive user demands. These facilities are essential for the digital economy, supporting everything from emails to online shopping, and their importance has grown with trends like remote work and emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. India is poised for significant growth in its data center industry, driven by government incentives and an increasing need for robust data storage and processing capabilities, despite environmental concerns related to energy consumption.

feed.title: Sonos Roam SL vs Sonos Roam: which Bluetooth speaker will be the best?
feed.summary: This article compares the Sonos Roam SL and the Sonos Roam, two portable Bluetooth speakers from Sonos, to help consumers decide which one best suits their needs. The key difference lies in the Roam having a built-in microphone for voice controls, Auto Trueplay, and Sound Swap, features absent from the more affordable Roam SL. Both speakers share the same design, battery life, and core audio technology, making the choice dependent on budget and the importance of smart features.

feed.title: Cloud management provider Cloocus receives $41 mn in Series B funding
feed.summary: Cloud management service provider Cloocus Co. has secured $40.8 million (50 billion won) in Series B funding from SK Inc. C&C as part of a larger 100 billion won round. This investment follows significant funding rounds for other Korean cloud MSPs like Megazone Cloud and Bespin Global. The capital injections reflect a turnaround for Korean MSPs, driven by increased demand for cloud services due to the pandemic and the growing adoption of SaaS and multicloud strategies.

feed.title: Your Fenty Beauty Favorites Are Now Available At Ulta Beauty
feed.summary: Rihanna's Fenty Beauty line is expanding its retail presence by launching in over 1,300 Ulta Beauty locations, both online and in-store, starting March 6th. This move aims to make the popular beauty brand more accessible to a wider audience, fulfilling Rihanna's vision of global inclusion. Fans can expect a sneak peek of available products on February 28th before the official launch.

feed.title: Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Stock Price Has Fallen 12.8% in 2022. Should You Buy It?
feed.summary: Alphabet's stock (GOOGL) has dropped 12.8% in 2022, leading many to question if it's a good buying opportunity. Despite plateauing ad revenues, Google is expanding into cloud services and cybersecurity, highlighted by its acquisition of Mandiant. The company is considered attractive at current prices, though antitrust concerns remain a risk.

feed.title: Rivian is sued by shareholder after rolling back electric vehicle price hikes
feed.summary: A shareholder has filed a lawsuit against Rivian Automotive Inc, alleging the company misled investors during its IPO by underpricing its electric vehicles. This alleged mispricing led to swift, unpopular price hikes that were later rolled back. The lawsuit claims these price adjustments tarnished Rivian's reputation and put preorders at risk.

feed.title: Starbucks, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo suspend operations in Russia; Amazon suspends web services sign-ups
feed.summary: Coca-Cola, Starbucks, PepsiCo, and Amazon have announced the suspension of their operations in Russia in response to the country's invasion of Ukraine. Coca-Cola stated it was pausing business, while Starbucks is suspending all business activity and closing stores. Amazon Web Services is no longer allowing new sign-ups in Russia or Belarus, emphasizing it does not have infrastructure there and will suspend services for those promoting violence.

feed.title: Shipping Fraud Increased Nearly 800% Worldwide in the Past Year
feed.summary: TransUnion's 2022 Global Digital Fraud Trends Report reveals that shipping fraud surged by 780.5% globally year-over-year in 2021, and over 1,500% from 2019 to 2021, making it the fastest-growing type of digital fraud worldwide. This increase is primarily attributed to the continuous growth of e-commerce, with fraudsters targeting areas where consumers are most active. The report also highlights significant increases in other fraud types and identifies industries most affected by digital fraud globally and in the United States, such as gaming, travel and leisure, and financial services.

feed.title: Rivian is sued for allegedly misleading investors about electric vehicle prices
feed.summary: Rivian Automotive Inc is facing a class-action lawsuit from a shareholder who claims the company misled investors by initially underpricing its electric vehicles, leading to unpopular price hikes that were later rolled back. The lawsuit alleges Rivian concealed that its R1S SUV and R1T pickup trucks were so underpriced they would require rapid price increases after its November IPO, damaging the company's reputation and risking pre-order cancellations. The plaintiff, Charles Larry Crews, cites the swift rollback of price increases and an apology from CEO R.J. Scaringe as "futile attempts at damage control."

feed.title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 billion buyback
feed.summary: Amazon announced its first stock split since 1999, proposing a 20-for-1 split that sent its stock soaring by 6% in extended trading. The company's board also authorized a share buyback program of up to $10 billion. This move follows similar stock splits by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Apple, and Tesla, aiming to make shares more accessible to investors and benefit employees.

feed.title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 bln share buyback
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. has announced a 20-for-1 stock split and authorized a $10 billion share buyback plan, causing its shares to rise by 7% in extended trading. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999, aimed at making shares more accessible to investors and increasing flexibility for employees managing equity. Trading with the new share price will commence on June 6.
